ogre-blade.description: A broad and heavy blade, the Ogre Blade is, much like its namesake, an unsubtle weapon.
ogre-blade.body: Armour Bane (1), Magical Attacks, Multiple Wounds (D3)

sword-of-battle.description: A simple weapon, yet finely crafted, blessed by mighty mages and revered priests.
sword-of-battle.body: Armour Bane (1), Extra Attacks (+1), Magical Attacks

meteor-hammer.description: No matter who wields this mighty hammer, their blows will land with the force of a meteor plummeting from the heavens.
meteor-hammer.body: Notes: When making a roll To Wound with this weapon, a roll of a 3+ is always a success, regardless of the target's Toughness.

spelleater-axe.description: Forged of rune-encrusted brass, the Spelleater Axe is anathema to the Winds of Magic.

hell-forged-axe.description: In the midst of battle, smoke billows and flames burst from the glowing blade of this fell weapon.

giant-blade.description: A broad and heavy blade wrought with powerful enchantments that only increase the weight of its blows, the Giant Blade is an unsubtle weapon.
giant-blade.body: Armour Bane (2), Magical Attacks, Multiple Wounds (2)

dragon-slaying-sword.description: A mighty blade, wielded by many great heroes in their endless quests to slay foul monsters.

berserker-blade.description: Quenched in the blood of untold fallen enemies, the Berserker Blade eternally hungers for battle.
berserker-blade.body: Notes: The wielder of the Berserker Blade is Impetuous.

sword-of-sorrow.description: Though it possesses no special properties when wielded in combat, it is said that a gesture with the Sword of Sorrow can pierce an enemy's heart from afar.
sword-of-sorrow.body: Notes: The Sword of Sorrow is a missile weapon; it cannot be used in combat. No Ward or Regeneration saves are permitted against wounds caused by the Sword of Sorrow.

sword-of-swiftness.description: Crafted from magically attuned materials and ensorcelled to strike as if with a life of its own.

sword-of-might.description: Bound around with powerful runes that increase its power and enhance the strength of its bearer.

biting-blade.description: The serrated length of the Biting Blade cuts through armour of plate and mail with terrible ease.

sword-of-striking.description: Engraved with runes of accuracy and swiftness, the Sword of Striking is an elegant weapon of great precision.
sword-of-striking.body:
Notes: During the Combat phase, the wielder of the Sword of Striking has a +1 modifier to their rolls To Hit.
*Extremely Common

cackling-blade.description: Those who carry the Cackling Blade relinquish all self control until the battle has long ended - often to their peril.
cackling-blade.body: Notes: If a natural 6 is rolled for the Extra Attacks (+D6) special rule, the wielder of the Cackling Blade immediately loses a single Wound.

armour-of-destiny.description: The potent Armour of Destiny protects its wearer from all but the most grievous of harm.
armour-of-destiny.body: The Armour of Destiny is a suit of heavy armour. In addition, its wearer has a 4+ Ward save against any wounds suffered.

burning-blade.description: Once unsheathed, the cutting edge of the Burning Blade writhes endlessly with a living flame.

armour-of-silvered-steel.description: Polished to a mirror shine, the Armour of Silvered Steel encases its wearer from head to toe.
armour-of-silvered-steel.body: The Armour of Silvered Steel is a suit of armour that gives its wearer an armour value of 3+ which cannot be improved in any way.

bedazzling-helm.description: A gleaming helm that confuses and confounds enemies, causing their blows to fall wide of their mark.
bedazzling-helm.body: Models whose troop type is infantry or cavalry only. May be worn with other armour. The wearer of the Bedazzling Helm improves their armour value by 1 (to a maximum of 2+). In addition, any enemy model that directs its attacks against the wearer during the Combat phase suffers a -1 modifier to its rolls To Hit.

glittering-scales.description: Each and every scale of this armoured surcoat is crafted from shards of precious metal.
glittering-scales.body: The Glittering Scales is a suit of light armour. In addition, once per turn, you may make your opponent re-roll a single roll To Hit made against the wearer.

shield-of-the-warrior-true.description: A heavy shield of oak and iron that turns aside all but the most deadly of missiles.
shield-of-the-warrior-true.body: The Shield of the Warrior True is a shield. In addition, its bearer has a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered during the Shooting phase.

levitating-shield.description: Born aloft by a cunning enchantment, this shield seems to place itself between its owner and the weapons of the enemy.
levitating-shield.body: Models whose troop type is infantry only. The Levitating Shield is a shield. In addition, the bearer may use it alongside a weapon with the Requires Two Hands special rule during combat.

spellshield.description: The Winds of Magic lose their power when in the presence of the brass-bound Spellshield.
spellshield.body:
The Spellshield is a shield. In addition, its bearer has a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by a Magic Missile, a Magical Vortex, or an Assailment spell.
*Extremely Common

armour-of-meteoric-iron.description: This heavy armour was forged of ore mined from a meteor that fell from the heavens.
armour-of-meteoric-iron.body: The Armour of Meteoric Iron gives its wearer an armour value of 5+, which cannot be improved in any way. However, nor can this armour value be reduced in any way either.

headsman-s-axe.description: A wide bladed axe, steeped in the blood of its countless helpless victims.
headsman-s-axe.body: Killing Blow, Magical Attacks, Requires Two Hands

enchanted-shield.description: A finely crafted and sturdy shield that protects its bearer from harm time and time again.
enchanted-shield.body:
The Enchanted Shield is a shield. In addition, its bearer has a 6+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by a non-magical enemy attack.
*Extremely Common

charmed-shield.description: A simple shield hung with charms and fetishes to bring the bearer good fortune. In the heat of battle, such ornamentation rarely survives intact for long.
charmed-shield.body:
The Charmed Shield is a shield. In addition, once per game the Charmed Shield gives its bearer a 5+ Ward save against a single wound. Once this Ward save has been used, the Charmed Shield is considered to be an ordinary, non magical shield.
*Extremely Common

icon-of-fortitude.description: Carefully woven with protective enchantments, this exquisite brooch is said to shield its bearer from the deadliest blows.
icon-of-fortitude.body: Models whose troop type is infantry or cavalry only. The bearer is immune to the Multiple Wounds (X) special rule. If the bearer is wounded by an attack with this special rule, they suffer a single wound.

dawnstone.description: The magic trapped within this semi-precious stone binds together shattered armour plates.
dawnstone.body: The bearer of the Dawnstone may re-roll any Armour Save roll of a natural 1.

talisman-of-protection.description: A powerful magical aura surrounds this humble talisman, protecting its wearer from harm.
talisman-of-protection.body: The Talisman of Protection gives its bearer a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered.

ironhide-talisman.description: It is said that the one who bears this powerful heirloom can endure even the most telling blows.
ironhide-talisman.body:
Models whose troop type is infantry only. Any enemy model that makes a successful roll To Hit against the bearer of the Ironhide Talisman during the Shooting phase or Combat phase must re-roll any rolls To Wound of a natural 6.
Note that this magic item does not work against attacks that hit automatically.

obsidian-lodestone.description: An air of chill hangs about obsidian, stilling the Winds of Magic in its presence.
obsidian-lodestone.body:
A model may purchase up to three Obsidian Lodestones. A model that bears a single Obsidian Lodestone has Magic Resistance (-1), a model that bears two has Magic Resistance (-2), and a model that bears three has Magic Resistance (-3).
*Extremely Common

paymaster-s-coin.description: This heavy golden coin may not be enchanted, but its weight in its owner's pocket certainly inspires heroism.
paymaster-s-coin.body:
Single use. The bearer of a Paymaster's Coin can re-roll any failed rolls To Hit made during the Combat phase.
*Extremely Common

luckstone.description: Can luck be trapped within a dull stone pendant? Possibly.
luckstone.body:
Single use. The bearer of a Luckstone can re-roll a single failed Armour Save roll.
*Extremely Common

banner-of-iron-resolve.description: No regiment that stands beneath the Banner of Iron Resolve has ever fled from the foe.
banner-of-iron-resolve.body: A unit carrying the Banner of Iron Resolve gains the Stubborn special rule.

banner-of-the-steadfast.description: Woven into the bright fabric of this banner is a scene of unimaginable gallantry, a scene that serves to inspire those who fight in its shadow to hold their ground no matter the odds.
banner-of-the-steadfast.body: Models whose troop type is infantry only. Should a unit carrying the Banner of the Steadfast belong to the losing side of a Combat, it can Fall Back in Good Order even if the Unit Strength of the winning side is more than twice that of its own side.

totem-of-wrath.description: Cruel runes etched into the surface of this icon tremble with power, causing those around it to succumb to an animalistic ferocity.
totem-of-wrath.body: During a turn in which it charged, models within a unit carrying the Totem of Wrath improve the Armour Piercing characteristic of their weapons by 1, and may re-roll any rolls To Wound of a natural 1.

razor-standard.description: Hung with hundreds of wickedly sharp blades, an air of sharpness radiates outwards from the Razor Standard.
razor-standard.body: A unit carrying the Razor Standard gains the Armour Bane (2) special rule.

banner-of-swirling-wind.description: Gale-force winds surge around this standard so fiercely that arrows and shot are blown forcefully away from their target.
banner-of-swirling-wind.body: Any enemy model that shoots at a unit carrying the Banner of Swirling Wind suffers an additional -1 To Hit modifier.

rampaging-banner.description: As a matter of honour, those that fight beneath the Rampaging Banner are always first into the fray.
rampaging-banner.body: When a unit carrying the Rampaging Banner declares a charge, it may re-roll its Charge roll.

the-blazing-banner.description: An eternal flame flickers about the weapons of those that march beneath the Blazing Banner.
the-blazing-banner.body: A unit carrying the Blazing Banner gains the Flaming Attacks special rule.

monster-hunter-s-tapestry.description: Those who have earned the right to fight under this standard have battled some of the Old World's most dangerous beasts and lived to tell the tale.
monster-hunter-s-tapestry.body: Enemy units may not make Stomp Attacks against a unit carrying the Monster Hunter's Tapestry.

war-banner.description: A proud banner of great age. Those that march beneath the War Banner fight with grim resolve.
war-banner.body: When calculating its combat result, a unit carrying the War Banner may claim an additional bonus of +1 combat result point.

wizarding-hat.description: This splendid hat, once the property of a long dead Wizard, is still haunted by their ghost.
wizarding-hat.body: The wearer is a Level 1 Wizard and knows one randomly generated spell from a Lore of Magic of your choosing. However, the whispers of the ghostly Wizard haunting the hat are often confusing. Therefore, the wearer also becomes subject to the Stupidity special rule.

duellist-s-blades.description: Fine weapons, forged by the greatest of swordsmiths and imbued with potent runes of quickening.
duellist-s-blades.body: Extra Attacks (+2), Magical Attacks, Requires Two Hands

arch-lightning-rod.description: Crackling lightning fills the heavens with peril, grounding the creatures of the sky.
arch-lightning-rod.body: Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, the bearer of the Arch-Lightning Rod may attempt to use it by making a Leadership test (using their own, unmodified Leadership). If this test is passed, until your next Start of Turn sub-phase enemy units cannot use the Fly (X) special rule.

flying-carpet.description: Woven from the finest silks in a far-off land, this splendid rug does more than warm the feet!
flying-carpet.body: Models whose troop type is regular infantry or heavy infantry only. The bearer of the Flying Carpet gains the Fly (8) and Swiftstride special rules. However, the bearer cannot join a unit.

ruby-ring-of-ruin.description: Uttering a simple command, the wearer of the ring can hurl a flaming ball of ruin at their foes.
ruby-ring-of-ruin.body: The wielder of the Ruby Ring of Ruin can cast the Fireball spell from the Lore of Battle Magic as a Bound spell, with a Power Level of 1.

healing-potion.description: Purveyors of magical potions make many bold claims. Sometimes they are true, sometimes not.
healing-potion.body:
Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, the bearer of a Healing Potion can consume it. The model immediately recovers D3 lost Wounds.
*Extremely Common

potion-of-fervour.description: This noxious brew allows those who risk drinking it a moment of godliness upon the battlefield.
potion-of-fervour.body:
Single Use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, the bearer of the Potion of Fervour can consume it. Until the end of that turn, the model has a +D3 modifier to its Attacks characteristic (to a maximum of 10).
Note that a model can only consume a single potion (of any type) per Command phase.

potion-of-strength.description: A concoction of strength-giving vegetables and roots, mixed together with a touch of magic.
potion-of-strength.body:
Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, the bearer of a Potion of Strength can consume it. Until the end of that turn, the model has a +D3 modifier to its Strength characteristic (to a maximum of 10).
*Extremely Common

potion-of-toughness.description: Distilled by magical means, this potion is sure to make the drinker all but invulnerable.
potion-of-toughness.body:
Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, the bearer of a Potion of Toughness can consume it. Until the end of that turn, the model has a +D3 modifier to its Toughness characteristic (to a maximum of 10).
*Extremely Common

becalming-orb.description: This pulsing crystal orb can syphon the Winds of Magic away from its bearer's enemies.
becalming-orb.body:
Single Use. The bearer of the Becalming Orb may cast the following Bound spell, with a Power level of 1:
Type | Hex
Casting Value | 8+
Range | Self
Until your next Start of Turn sub-phase, enemy Wizards that are within 15" of the caster when attempting to cast a spell must increase that spell's casting value by 2.

potion-of-speed.description: A powerful potion with a terrible aftertaste that sharpens the wits and speeds the reactions.
potion-of-speed.body:
Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, the bearer of a Potion of Speed can consume it. Until the end of that turn, the model has a +D3 modifier to its Initiative characteristic (to a maximum of 10).
*Extremely Common

potion-of-foolhardiness.description: A magical brew that fills the drinker with courage… it may actually just be strong liquor.
potion-of-foolhardiness.body:
Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, the bearer of a Potion of Foolhardiness can consume it. Until the end of that turn, the model gains the Immune To Psychology special rule.
*Extremely Common

trailblazer-s-hauberk.description: The local flora seems to shift and bend to allow the wearer to pass unimpeded through even the thickest briar.
trailblazer-s-hauberk.body: Models whose troop type is infantry only. The Trailblazer's Hauberk is a suit of heavy armour. In addition, its wearer gains the Move Through Cover and Scouts special rules.

scroll-of-transmogrification.description: For a Wizard, there are few things better than the rush of joy felt upon turning a rival into a frog!
scroll-of-transmogrification.body:
Single use. The bearer may use this scroll instead of making a Wizardly dispel attempt. The spell is cast as normal. Once the spell has been resolved, the casting player must roll equal to or lower than the casting Wizard's Level of Wizardry on a single D6. Should they fail, the Wizard turns into a frog.
Whilst transmogrified, the Wizard cannot cast or dispel any spells, cannot use any of their equipment (magical or mundane) and reduces all of their characteristics (excluding Wounds) to 1. During each Start of Turn sub-phase, a player may roll a D6 for each transmogrified Wizard in their army. On a roll of 4+, the Wizard returns to normal (but retains a love of water).
*Extremely Common

feedback-scroll.description: When read aloud, this charm causes ætheric energy to flood back towards the enemy Wizard.
feedback-scroll.body: Single use. The bearer may use this scroll instead of making a Wizardly dispel attempt. The spell is cast as normal. Once the spell has been resolved, roll two D6. For each roll of a 4+, the casting Wizard loses a single Wound.

wand-of-jet.description: Carved from brittle jet, this wand refines a Wizard's power, but is easily broken.
wand-of-jet.body:
The bearer of the Wand of Jet may apply a +1 modifier to any of their Casting or Dispel rolls. However, should they roll any natural double when making a Casting or Dispel roll, the Wand of Jet is destroyed and it cannot be used again.
Note that this is a modifier to the result of a roll – it does not negate a roll of a natural double 1.

staff-of-quietude.description: With a gesture, the bearer of the Staff of Quietude calms the Winds of Magic, causing spells and conjurations to dissipate into the other.
staff-of-quietude.body: During the Command sub-phase of their turn, the bearer of the Staff of Quietude can attempt to unleash its power by making a Leadership test. If this test is passed, all Remains in Play spells currently in play are dispelled, including spells cast by friendly models.

lore-familiar.description: By creating a magical homunculus, a Wizard is able to better recall forgotten details of their studies.
lore-familiar.body: The owner of a Lore Familiar does not randomly generate their spells. Instead, they may choose which spells they know from their chosen lore (including that lore's signature spell).

power-scroll.description: Unfurling a scroll bearing runes of power can greatly increase the spell's power.
power-scroll.body:
Single use. A Wizard may use this scroll when attempting to cast a spell. If they do so, roll an extra D6 when making the Casting roll and discard the lowest result. However, if a double 1 is rolled on any two of the dice rolled, the spell is miscast.
*Extremely Common

tome-of-spellcraft.description: Reading aloud from a dusty tome of great age, the Wizard enunciates their spells with unrivalled clarity and precision.
tome-of-spellcraft.body:
Once per turn, the bearer of the Tome of Spellcraft may re-roll a Casting roll.
*Note all dice are re-rolled, including any bonus or discard dice granted by special rules or magic items.

scroll-of-disruption.description: When spoken aloud, the words upon this ancient scroll cause the Winds of Magic to bluster and the spells of the enemy to unravel.
scroll-of-disruption.body:
Once per turn, the bearer of the Scroll of Disruption may re-roll a Dispel roll.
*Note all dice are re-rolled, including any bonus or discard dice granted by special rules or magic items.

dispel-scroll.description: The Wizard reads aloud a charm of unbinding from an enchanted scroll.
dispel-scroll.body:
Single use. A Wizard may use this scroll when attempting a Wizardly dispel. If they do so, roll an extra D6 when making the Dispel roll and discard the lowest result. However, if a double 1 is rolled on any two of the dice rolled, the Wizard is outclassed in the art.
*Extremely Common

arcane-familiar.description: Many Wizards are accompanied by familiars gifted with arcane knowledge. These creatures constantly whisper secrets to their master.
arcane-familiar.body: The owner of an Arcane Familiar knows spells from two Lores of Magic, rather than the usual one. When determining the spells the Wizard knows, you must roll for each Lore separately. Duplicate spells are re-rolled as normal. The Wizard may discard one randomly generated spell as normal, replacing it with the signature spell of the same Lore of Magic.

earthing-rod.description: Inert metal runs the length of the Wizard's staff, drawing magical overloads safely into the earth.
earthing-rod.body: Single use. Should they miscast a spell, a Wizard can use the Earthing Rod to re-roll the result rolled on the Miscast table.

sword-of-heroes.description: This mighty blade has powerful enchantments against evil bound into it. Its long and bloody history has seen its wielders kill enough fantastical creatures to fill a menagerie many times over.
sword-of-heroes.body: Notes: When making a roll To Wound for a hit caused with the Sword of Heroes, a roll of 5+ is always a success, regardless of the target's Toughness.

sword-of-the-quest.description: This large hand-and-a-half sword has been passed down from knight to knight, aiding generations of heroes on their noble quests.
sword-of-the-quest.body:
Single-Handed:
Double-Handed:
Notes: The Sword of the Quest has two profiles. You must choose which the wielder will use at the start of each round of a combat.

heartwood-lance.description: This unbreakable lance is crafted from the heart of the Major Oak, the largest tree in Bretonnia, which was shattered by lightning the moment Gilles was struck down.
heartwood-lance.body: Notes: Models whose troop type is cavalry or monster only. The Heartwood Lance can only be used during a turn in which the wielder charged. In subsequent turns (or if the wielder did not charge) the model must use its hand weapon instead.

morning-star-of-fracasse.description: This mighty morning star has a hatred of magical trickery and unholy artefacts. It will entangle and rip a magic weapon from the hands of any foe.
morning-star-of-fracasse.body: Notes: Any magic weapon carried by an enemy model that suffers one or more unsaved wounds from the Morning Star of Fracasse is destroyed and cannot be used for the remainder of the game.

sword-of-the-stout-hearted.description: Imbued with the courage of Gilles le Breton himself, this sword fills the wielder with the fortitude to face down any enemy.
sword-of-the-stout-hearted.body: Armour Bane (1), Immune to Psychology, Magical Attacks, Requires Two Hands

frontier-axe.description: Enchanted to ensure it never lost its razor-sharp edge while felling lumber, this tool, turned weapon of war, can sever limbs and sunder armour in a single swing.
frontier-axe.body: Notes: The Frontier Axe may only be taken by a model in a Bretonnian Exiles Army of Infamy.

foebreaker.description: Even those tough enough to survive a pummeling from this mighty warhammer are left disoriented and staggered by its heavy blows, making them vulnerable to any further onslaught.
foebreaker.body: Notes: Any enemy model that suffers one or more unsaved wounds from the Foebreaker must immediately make a Toughness test. If the test is failed, the wounded model suffers a -1 modifier to its Weapon Skill and Attacks characteristics (to a minimum of 1) until the end of the next Combat phase.

gilded-cuirass.description: Inscribed with the words of the Grail Vow, the blessings of the Lady shine upon the wearer.
gilded-cuirass.body: The Gilded Cuirass is a suit of heavy armour. In addition, its wearer has the Regeneration (5+) special rule.

gromril-great-helm.description: This ornate helm, a gift from the Dwarf King Grundhar, bears a potent rune of protection.
gromril-great-helm.body: May be worn with other armour. The wearer of the Gromril Great Helm improves their armour value by 1 (to a maximum of 2+). In addition, the wearer may re-roll any roll of a natural 1 made when making an Armour Save roll.

ironspike-shield.description: Covered in large, sharpened spines, this deadly looking shield is as dangerous as any mace.
ironspike-shield.body: The Ironspike Shield may only be taken by a model in a Bretonnian Exiles Army of Infamy. The Ironspike Shield is a shield. Whenever an opponent rolls a natural 1 To Hit or To Wound the wielder of the Ironspike Shield in combat, they immediately suffer a Strength 3 hit with an AP of -1.

anointed-armour.description: Whilst the wearer's faith in the Lady of the Lake holds fast, so too shall the wards of protection placed upon this armour.
anointed-armour.body: Models with the Grail Vow whose troop type is infantry or cavalry only. The Anointed Armour is a suit of heavy armour. In addition, as long as the wearer has the Blessing of the Lady, they are immune to the Killing Blow and Multiple Wounds (X) special rules. If the wearer suffers an unsaved wound from an attack with either of these special rules, they lose a single Wound. Should the wearer ever lose the Blessing of the Lady, this effect is lost.

grail-pendant.description: The power of the Lady floods through her most devoted warriors, giving them strength to endure the most grievous wounds.
grail-pendant.body: Models with the Grail Vow only. Single use. When the wearer of the Grail Pendant loses their last Wound, roll a D6. On a roll of 2+, the Wound is not lost.

mantle-of-the-damsel-elena.description: Legend has it that Elena continued fighting the Goblin hordes even as the venom of a thousand spider bites coursed through her veins.
mantle-of-the-damsel-elena.body: The bearer is immune to the Poisoned Attacks special rule. If the bearer is wounded by an attack with this special rule, the attacker must roll To Wound as normal.

valorous-standard.description: Knights who ride under this banner sing lustily and cry in joy for the sheer love of battle.
valorous-standard.body: A unit carrying the Valorous Standard rolls 3D6 when making a Break test and discards the highest result.

lucky-heirloom.description: Though it may appear as junk to others, some warriors dare not enter the fray without some charm they had about their person when they first escaped death.
lucky-heirloom.body:
A Lucky Heirloom may only be taken by a model in a Bretonnian Exiles Army of Infamy. Once per round, the bearer of the Lucky Heirloom can re-roll a single failed roll To Hit or To Wound, or re-roll a failed Armour Save or Ward Save roll.
*Extremely Common

errantry-banner.description: This tattered banner has travelled the length and breadth of the Old World and beyond, instilling its bearers with fiery zeal.
errantry-banner.body: All models in a unit carrying the Errantry Banner have a +1 modifier to their Strength characteristic during a turn in which they charge. However, the unit also gains the Impetuous special rule.

crusader-s-lance.description: In the hands of young Bretonnian heroes throughout the kingdom's many errantry wars, this keen lance has struck down scores of Orcs, Goblins and Beastmen.
crusader-s-lance.body: Notes: The Crusader's Lance may only be taken by a model in an Errantry Crusade Army of Infamy whose troop type is cavalry or monster only. The Crusader's Lance can only be used during a turn in which the wielder charged. In subsequent turns (or if the wielder did not charge), the model must use its hand weapon instead.

banner-of-honourable-warfare.description: Though no knight would ever take to the field of battle with bow or sling, those who fight under the banner pursue those who do with extreme prejudice.
banner-of-honourable-warfare.body: A unit carrying the Banner of Honourable Warfare must re-roll any failed rolls To Hit made during the first round of combat when engaged with an enemy equipped with any missile weapons.

banner-of-the-zealous-knight.description: Filled with religious vigour, those who ride into battle under this imposing standard are eager to close with the enemy as swiftly as possible.
banner-of-the-zealous-knight.body: The Banner of the Zealous Knight may only be taken by a model in a Bretonnian Exiles Army of Infamy. A unit carrying the Banner of the Zealous Knight gains the Vanguard special rule.

antlers-of-the-great-hunt.description: The knight's helm is adorned with a splendid set of antlers, the quarry of a great hunt slain by the wearer. The antlers denote exceptional prowess as a horseman and hunter.
antlers-of-the-great-hunt.body: If the wearer of the Antlers of the Great Hunt is mounted on a Barded Warhorse or a Warhorse, they and any unit they join gains the Move Through Cover special rule.

sirienne-s-locket.description: Sirienne, as skilled at conventional arts as she was at the art of magic, crafted this exquisite charm into a likeness of the Lady.
sirienne-s-locket.body: Models whose troop type is infantry or cavalry only. The bearer is immune to the Multiple Wounds (X) special rule. If the bearer is wounded by an attack with this special rule, they suffer a single wound.

gauntlet-of-the-duel.description: When cast down, this enchanted gauntlet magnifies even the tiniest scrap of pride or conceit into a surge of righteous self-belief.
gauntlet-of-the-duel.body:
Challenges issued by the bearer of a Gauntlet of the Duel cannot be refused.
*Extremely Common

conqueror-s-tapestry.description: The morning after a battle, the victorious knights awaken to find their exploits depicted within this enchanted tapestry.
conqueror-s-tapestry.body: Any enemy standard captured by a unit carrying the Conqueror's Tapestry is worth 100 Victory Points as a trophy of war.

the-seal-of-parravon.description: Those with the skill-at-arms to win the famed tourney of Parravon are masters of their chosen weapons and carry the Seal of Parravon as a token of their victory.
the-seal-of-parravon.body: When the bearer of the Seal of Parravon makes a roll To Hit, a roll of a 3+ is always a success, regardless of the target's Weapon Skill.

wyrmbreath-vial.description: By consuming the deep red liquid contained within this vial, it is said that the drinker can summon forth the fury of the great Dragons that dwell in the mountain ranges surrounding the Border Princes.
wyrmbreath-vial.body: A Wyrmbreath Vial may only be taken by a model in a Bretonnian Exiles Army of Infamy. Single Use. The Wyrmbreath Vial is a breath weapon with the following profile:

banner-of-the-lady-s-grace.description: This finely crafted standard depicts the Lady's first meeting with Gilles le Breton, the first king of Bretonnia, inspiring courage and valour in all who fight alongside it.
banner-of-the-lady-s-grace.body: A unit carrying the Banner of the Lady's Grace ignores all negative modifiers to its Leadership characteristic.

crusader-s-tapestry.description: Those that fight beneath this silken banner are inspired to ever greater acts of heroism, hoping that maybe their own exploits will be woven into its rich history.
crusader-s-tapestry.body: The Crusader's Tapestry may only be taken by a model in an Errantry Crusade Army of Infamy. A unit carrying the Crusader's Tapestry gains the Frenzy special rule.

silver-mirror.description: This lethal trinket is at first sight merely a vanity mirror, but woe betide the magic user that underestimates its true abilities...
silver-mirror.body: Single use. The bearer of the Silver Mirror may use it when attempting a Wizardly dispel. If they do so, roll an extra D6 when making the Dispel roll and discard the lowest result. If a double 1 is rolled on any two of the dice rolled, the bearer is outclassed in the art and the dispel attempt fails. If the dispel attempt is successful, the spell is dispelled and the casting Wizard suffers a Strength 4 hit with an AP of -2.

sacrament-of-the-lady.description: These thin, translucent wafers have been blessed by the Lady herself and imbued with a fragment of her power.
sacrament-of-the-lady.body:
Single use. The bearer of a Sacrament of the Lady may use it before making a Casting roll. If they do, they may apply a +2 modifier to that Casting roll.
Note that this is a modifier to the result of a roll – it does not negate a roll of a natural double 1.
*Extremely Common

heart-of-the-wilds.description: Gifted to Damsel Elliea long ago by the Wood Elves of Athel Loren, this thrumming, mossy stone flows with magical power, drawing upon the strength of nature to fuel its wielder's arcane efforts.
heart-of-the-wilds.body: The bearer of the Heart of the Wilds may apply a +1 modifier to any of their Casting rolls whilst within any 'natural' terrain feature. For the purposes of this rule, a 'natural' terrain feature includes any woods, or any difficult or dangerous terrain. It does not include any constructions, such as walls or buildings. Before the game starts, the players should agree upon which terrain features are natural and which are not.

prayer-icon-of-quenelles.description: When opened, this prayer icon displays a meticulously rendered image of the Lady that inspires unfettered devotion.
prayer-icon-of-quenelles.body: The bearer of the Prayer Icon of Quenelles increases their Dispel range by 3". Additionally, when attempting to dispel a Hex spell, the bearer of the Prayer Icon of Quenelles gains a +1 modifier to their Dispel roll.

flamestrike-wand.description: Crafted from the charred branch of an ancient oak that was almost totally consumed in a forest fire, this wand allows the bearer to summon forth that same devastating inferno.
flamestrike-wand.body: The Flamestrike Wand may only be taken by a model in a Bretonnian Exiles Army of Infamy. Single Use. The bearer of the Flamestrike Wand may cast the Fireball spell from the Lore of Battle Magic as a Bound spell with a Power Level of 3.

diadem-of-power.description: When accompanying their baron's knights into battle, damsels and prophetesses have donned this jewel-studded band to help them channel the more destructive power that they wield in order to smite the Lady's enemies.
diadem-of-power.body: The Diadem of Power may only be taken by a model in an Errantry Crusade Army of Infamy. When attempting to cast a Magical Vortex, Magic Missile or an Assailment spell, the bearer of the Diadem of Power gains a +1 modifier to their Casting roll.

virtue-of-knightly-temper.description: With a heart of stone and resolute temper Beren stood unbowed, each sweep of blade spilling the blood of many.
virtue-of-knightly-temper.body: During a turn in which it charged, a model with this Virtue gains the Extra Attacks (+D3) and Hatred (all enemies) special rules.

virtue-of-heroism.description: Known as the Slayer of Monsters, Gilles fought and killed many great beasts that stalked the Massif Orcal, mounting their heads on the walls of his fastness.
virtue-of-heroism.body: Unless using a magic weapon, a model with this Virtue gains the Killing Blow and Monster Slayer special rules.

banner-of-ch-lons.description: Awestruck enemies are unable to tear their gaze away from this magnificent banner.
banner-of-ch-lons.body: Enemy units cannot declare a Stand & Shoot charge reaction against a unit carrying the Banner of Châlons.

virtue-of-the-penitent.description: A penitent hermit-knight, Duke Corduin set aside his vows of solitude when summoned to fight for his king.
virtue-of-the-penitent.body: Duke, Baron or Paladin only. A character with this Virtue gains the Unbreakable special rule. However, this character cannot join a friendly unit.

virtue-of-audacity.description: A master of feint and riposte, Agilgar's skill at turning an enemy's skill against them was legendary.
virtue-of-audacity.body: A model with this Virtue may re-roll any failed rolls To Hit made against an enemy model with a higher Weapon Skill characteristic than it.

crusader-s-clarion.description: Upon hearing the sound of this gilded trumpet, the warhorses beneath the gallant knights of Bretonnia thunder into battle with renewed strength and vigour.
crusader-s-clarion.body: The Crusader's Clarion may only be taken by a model in an Errantry Crusade Army of Infamy that is mounted on a Bretonnian Warhorse only. On a turn in which the bearer of the Crusader's Clarion charged, their mount and all mounts in the unit they have joined have a +1 modifier to their Strength characteristic.

virtue-of-duty.description: Most loyal of Companions, brave Duke Thierulf of Lyonesse did lament most painfully when Gilles did fall...
virtue-of-duty.body: Duke, Baron or Paladin only. Unless the General of their army has been removed from play as a casualty, when calculating its combat result, this character may claim a bonus of +1 combat result point. This character cannot be your army General or join a friendly unit.

virtue-of-stoicism.description: Awe inspiring are the tales that tell of grim Lambard, standing alone against evil hordes to save his dukedom.
virtue-of-stoicism.body: A model with this Virtue (and its unit) may re-roll the 2D6 when making a Break test.

virtue-of-the-ideal.description: Unmatched was Landuin, his chivalry above all others. Alas, as great was his skill, so too was his arrogance.
virtue-of-the-ideal.body: Duke, Baron or Paladin only. A character with this Virtue has a +1 modifier to its Weapon Skill, Initiative, Attacks and Leadership characteristics. However, this character cannot be your army's General or join a friendly unit.

virtue-of-purity.description: Chaste and untainted by base emotions, Duke Rademund was the Lady's most virtuous champion.
virtue-of-purity.body: A model with this Virtue always benefits from the Blessings of the Lady special rule and always has a 5+ Ward save, even if this model's army did not pray at the start of the game.

virtue-of-confidence.description: Haughty, proud and skilful, Carleond of Couronne took never a backward step in the face of adversity.
virtue-of-confidence.body: A model with this Virtue must always issue and accept challenges (if possible). During a challenge, this model may re-roll any failed rolls To Hit.

virtue-of-the-joust.description: Great was Duke Folgar of Artois' skill at the tilt. None could withstand the thrust of his lance.
virtue-of-the-joust.body: A model with this Virtue may re-roll any failed rolls To Wound made when using a lance.

falcon-horn-of-fredemund.description: This ancient horn was used by the Grail Companion, Duke Fredemund of Aquitaine. When blown, it emits a piercing cry, and the skies become filled with flocks of hunting birds.
falcon-horn-of-fredemund.body: Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, the bearer of the Falcon-horn of Fredemund may attempt to use it by making a Leadership test (using their own unmodified Leadership). If this test is passed, until your next Start of Turn sub-phase enemy units cannot use the Fly (X) special rule.

virtue-of-the-impetuous-knight.description: In the glory of the charge was Balduin most alive. Though others better controlled their ardour, he was ever in the forefront of battle.
virtue-of-the-impetuous-knight.body: A model with this Virtue gains the Impetuous special rule. In addition, this model (and its unit) increases its maximum possible charge range by 3". Finally, when this model (and its unit) makes a Charge roll, you may apply a +D3 modifier to the result.

virtue-of-noble-disdain.description: Fredemund held in pure contempt those that would strike at their enemy from afar with a coward's weapon.
virtue-of-noble-disdain.body: A model with this Virtue may re-roll any failed rolls To Hit made during the first round of combat when engaged with an enemy equipped with any missile weapons.

runefang.description: At the dawn of the Empire, a dozen magical blades were forged for Sigmar's chieftains. Those that survive are treasured artefacts, potent symbols of the status and authority of their wielders.
runefang.body: Notes: When making a roll To Wound for a hit caused with a Runefang, a roll of 2+ is always a success, regardless of the target's Toughness.

virtue-of-discipline.description: Famed for his discipline, Marcus took to the field of battle undaunted by his enemies.
virtue-of-discipline.body: A model with this Virtue (and its unit) can march whilst within 8" of an enemy unit without first having to make a Leadership test.

mace-of-helsturm.description: This mace was used in battle by the first Grand Theogonist, Johann Helsturm. It is said that Helsturm's faith in Sigmar was strong enough to shatter the walls of a castle.
mace-of-helsturm.body:
Single-Handed:
Double-Handed:
Notes: The Mace of Helsturm has two profiles. You must choose which the wielder will use at the start of each round of a combat. If used double-handed, the wielder may make only one attack, regardless of their Attacks characteristic.

virtue-of-empathy.description: A champion of the people, Martrud fought shoulder to shoulder with the peasants he protected.
virtue-of-empathy.body: Duke, Baron or Paladin only. A character with this Virtue can join a unit with the Peasantry special rule.

sword-of-justice.description: The Sword of Justice is an ancient weapon studded with Dwarf runes of vengeance and retribution that bestow the power of unswerving accuracy and deadly retribution upon it.
sword-of-justice.body: Notes: The wielder of the Sword of Justice may re-roll any failed rolls To Wound.

blade-of-silvered-steel.description: Those who wield this blessed weapon will hunt the dead and the damned with unmatched zeal.
blade-of-silvered-steel.body: Notes: The Blade of Silvered Steel may only be taken by a model in a Knightly Order Army of Infamy. Undead models cannot make Armour or Regeneration saves against a wound caused by this weapon.

hammer-of-righteousness.description: This mighty hammer not only crushes flesh and bone but shatters evil with each swing.
hammer-of-righteousness.body: Notes: Models hit by the Hammer of Righteousness must make a Leadership test for each hit suffered. If the test is failed, the hit wounds automatically and no Armour save is allowed (Regeneration and Ward saves may be taken as normal). If the test is passed, rolls To Wound and Armour saves are made as normal.

pearl-daggers.description: Forged from burnished steel that glitters in the sunlight, the wielder of these lightweight daggers strikes with deadly speed and precision.
pearl-daggers.body: Notes: The wielder of the Pearl Daggers may re-roll any failed rolls To Hit during the Combat phase.

dragon-bow.description: A relic from the ancient Elven colonies of the Old World, this wondrously crafted bow enables the wielder to outshoot the finest archers in the Empire.
dragon-bow.body: Notes: Commanders of the Empire only.

shield-of-the-gorgon.description: This burnished shield harnesses the petrifying power of the monstrous gorgons that inhabit the deserts of Araby.
shield-of-the-gorgon.body: The Shield of the Gorgon is a shield that may only be taken by a model in a Knightly Order Army of Infamy. In addition, whilst in base contact with the bearer, enemy models suffer a -1 modifier to their Attacks characteristic (to a minimum of 1).

armour-of-fortune.description: Engraved with runes of luck and providence, the Armour of Fortune turns aside fatal blows harmlessly.
armour-of-fortune.body: The Armour of Fortune is a suit of heavy armour. In addition, its wearer has a 6+ Ward save against any wounds suffered and is immune to the Killing Blow special rule. If the wearer is struck a Killing Blow, they are permitted armour and Regeneration saves as normal. If the wound is unsaved, they lose a single Wound.

armour-of-tarnus.description: This cunning armour was crafted to the specifications of the warrior-Wizard von Tarnus.
armour-of-tarnus.body: The Armour of Tarnus is a suit of light armour which may be purchased and worn by an Imperial Wizard, even if they do not have the option to be equipped with armour, a shield or barding, without penalty. In addition, its wearer has a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered.

jade-amulet.description: Potent jade talismans are given in thanks for services performed on behalf of the Cult of Sigmar.
jade-amulet.body:
The bearer is immune to the Killing Blow special rule. If the bearer is struck a Killing Blow, they are permitted armour and Regeneration saves as normal. If the wound is unsaved, they lose a single Wound.
*Extremely Common

twice-blessed-armour.description: Enchanted with magic and blessed by righteous hands, this armour stands as an example of what a unified Empire can achieve.
twice-blessed-armour.body: The Twice-blessed Armour is a suit of full plate armour. In addition, the wearer may cast the Hammerhand spell from the Lore of Battle Magic as a Bound spell with a Power Level of 2.

the-white-cloak.description: Blessed by Ar-Ulric, the magics within this fine cloak protect the wearer from the hottest flame.
the-white-cloak.body: The wearer of the White Cloak has a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered, and a 3+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by an attack that has the Flaming Attacks special rule.

banner-of-the-knights-panther.description: The honour of bearing the heirloom banner of the Knights Panther into battle is known to only a few courageous individuals.
banner-of-the-knights-panther.body: Battle Standard Bearer belonging to the Order of the Knights Panther only. A unit carrying the Banner of the Knights Panther gains the Unbreakable special rule.

imperial-banner.description: This fine silken standard is a proud reminder of a time when the Empire was unified as one.
imperial-banner.body: All friendly units within the Command range of the model carrying the Imperial Banner roll 3D6 when making a Fear, Panic or Terror test and discard the highest result.

the-gleaming-pennant.description: Shining with an inner radiance, the Gleaming Pennant offers hope to those that march beneath it.
the-gleaming-pennant.body:
Single use. A unit carrying the Gleaming Pennant may re-roll a single failed Leadership test.
Note that a Break test is not a Leadership test.

griffon-standard.description: A unit flying the Griffon Standard resolutely stands its ground, and few foes can break them.
griffon-standard.body: When determining your combat result, a unit carrying the Griffon Standard can claim a Rank Bonus of +2 for each extra rank behind the first, rather than the usual +1.

icon-of-morr.description: The spine-chilling influence of the god of death can be felt most keenly around this macabre totem.
icon-of-morr.body: A unit carrying the Icon of Morr gains the Fear special rule. If they already have the Fear special rule, they instead gain the Terror special rule.

von-trickschotte-s-wondrous-arquebus.description: This huge weapon shoots large calibre rounds capable of shattering a Troll's skull with a single shot.
von-trickschotte-s-wondrous-arquebus.body: Notes: Von Trickschotte's Wondrous Arquebus may only be taken by a model in a City-state of Nuln Army of Infamy. The wielder of this weapon does not suffer the usual -1 modifier for shooting at long range.

banner-of-duty.description: This venerable banner steels the hearts of despairing warriors, renewing their will to fight on.
banner-of-duty.body: A unit carrying the Banner of Duty may re-roll any failed Rally test.

ring-of-fortune.description: Though soldiers are encouraged not to be superstitious or carry lucky charms, even experienced commanders know not to tempt fate.
ring-of-fortune.body: Single use. The bearer of the Ring of Fortune can re-roll any failed rolls To Wound made during the Combat phase.

laurels-of-victory.description: Celebrated heroes of the Empire are decorated with golden laurels which magnify their fearsome reputation in the eyes of their enemies.
laurels-of-victory.body: When determining your combat result, each unsaved wound caused by an attack made by the bearer of the Laurels of Victory (but not their mount) is worth 2 combat result points, rather than the usual 1.

the-banner-of-the-free-state-of-nuln.description: The City-state of Nuin has no stake in the War of the Three Emperors, instead taking pride in the prosperity of their great city.
the-banner-of-the-free-state-of-nuln.body: The Banner of the Free State of Nuln may only be taken by a model in a City-state of Nuln Army of Infamy. A unit carrying the Banner of the Free State of Nuln gains the Stubborn special rule.

the-silver-horn.description: The triumphant call of this elegant hunting horn lends speed to the hooves of even the weariest steed.
the-silver-horn.body: Characters with the Swiftstride special rule only. The bearer of the Silver Horn (and any unit they have joined) may re-roll the D6 when using the Swiftstride special rule.

ring-of-taal.description: By evoking the name of Taal, the primordial god of the wilderness, the wearer shields themselves in nature's grasp.
ring-of-taal.body: Single use. The bearer of the Ring of Taal may cast the Oaken Shield spell from the Lore of Battle Magic as a Bound spell with a Power Level of 3.

book-of-ashur.description: Written by an Elven Mage, this comprehensive book of magic is a priceless text for those that practice the art of magic... unless this copy is a poorly proofread and badly edited reproduction, that is.
book-of-ashur.body: The bearer of the Book of Ashur increases their Dispel range by 3" and, unless they roll any natural double, may apply a +1 modifier to any of their Casting or Dispel rolls. However, if the bearer rolls any natural double when making a Casting or Dispel roll, the book has proven to be a poor reproduction, full of glaring errors, and the +1 modifier cannot be applied to that roll.

witch-hunter-s-ward.description: The hunters of witches have long carried blessed trinkets to shield them from the evils they stalk.
witch-hunter-s-ward.body:
A model that bears a Witch Hunter's Ward has the Magic Resistance (-2) special rule. In addition, once per game, the bearer of a Witch Hunter's Ward can re-roll a single failed Armour Save roll.
*Extremely Common

shroud-of-iron.description: This strange device resembles a market trader's awning. When unfurled, the Shroud of Iron protects its bearer from harm falling from on high.
shroud-of-iron.body: The bearer of the Shroud of Iron (and any unit they have joined) has a 6+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by a non-magical template.

tome-of-midnight.description: As Wizards are often left to pursue their own paths to power, many end up perusing texts unfit for mortal minds.
tome-of-midnight.body: The bearer of the Tome of Midnight may apply a +1 modifier to any of their Casting rolls when attempting to cast spells from the Lore of Daemonology, Dark Magic or Necromancy. In addition, they know one more spell (chosen in the usual way) than is normal for their Level of Wizardry. However, the bearer can only cast a number of spells equal to their Level of Wizardry per turn and is subject to the Loner special rule.

twin-tailed-wand.description: Though its origin is unknown, this impractical wand allows its bearer to unleash a torrent of magical force.
twin-tailed-wand.body: Once per turn, the bearer of the Twin-tailed Wand may attempt to cast one of their spells a second time. However, should they miscast a spell, the bearer is overwhelmed by the Winds of Magic and, instead of rolling on the Miscast table, suffers D3 wounds with no armour or Regeneration saves permitted (Ward saves can be attempted as normal).

slayer-s-hourglass.description: As the sand tumbles through the hourglass, the decapitating strikes and snapping jaws of monstrous beasts become sluggish and slow.
slayer-s-hourglass.body: Enemy models whose troop type is monster suffer a -1 modifier to their Weapon Skill characteristic whilst in base contact with the bearer of the Slayer's Hourglass.

crystal-ball.description: Wizards who serve at court often rely upon reading portents and divining the future in order to best advise their masters.
crystal-ball.body: Once per turn, you may make your opponent re-roll a single roll To Hit or To Wound made against a friendly character model that is within the Command range of the bearer of the Crystal Ball.

master-rune-of-alaric-the-mad.description: Alaric the Mad forged the famous Runefangs for the Elector Counts of the Empire before meeting an unknown fate.
master-rune-of-alaric-the-mad.body: No armour save is permitted against wounds caused by a weapon inscribed with the Master Rune of Alaric the Mad (Ward and Regeneration saves can be attempted as normal).

master-rune-of-skalf-blackhammer.description: Runesmith Skalf forged many hammers of great might, and some maintain that even the hammer of Sigmar, Ghal Maraz itself, was his work.
master-rune-of-skalf-blackhammer.body: When making a roll To Wound with a weapon inscribed with the Master Rune of Skalf Blackhammer, a roll of 2+ is always a success, regardless of the target's Toughness.

tapestry-of-sigmar-s-triumph.description: Depicting Sigmar's heroic victories, this standard inspires others to meet the enemies of the Empire with weapons in-hand.
tapestry-of-sigmar-s-triumph.body: A unit carrying the Tapestry of Sigmar's Triumph may re-roll any rolls To Wound of a natural 1 during the first round of a combat.

master-rune-of-dragon-slaying.description: With this mighty rune the Dwarfs have slain many great wyrms and foul creatures of Chaos.
master-rune-of-dragon-slaying.body: When making a roll To Wound against an enemy whose troop type is behemoth with a weapon inscribed with the Master Rune of Dragon Slaying, a roll of 2+ is always a success, regardless of the target's Toughness.

master-rune-of-flight.description: This cunning rune has been used to surprise the Dwarfs' foes from afar since the world was young.
master-rune-of-flight.body: Hand weapon only. Once per turn, during the Shooting phase, a weapon inscribed with the Master Rune of Flight can be thrown with the following profile (which may be modified by additional runes):

squintsoffen-s-marvellous-magnifier.description: Popularised by its namesake, this pocket-sized spyglass allows the bearer to more easily target distant enemies on the battlefield.
squintsoffen-s-marvellous-magnifier.body: A Squintsoffen's Marvellous Magnifier may only be taken by models in a City-state of Nuln Army of Infamy. The bearer of a Magnifier and any unit they have joined does not suffer the usual -1 To Hit modifier when shooting at Long Range.

master-rune-of-smiting.description: The secret of this rune was preserved in the Rundrokikron, an ancient tome kept in the treasure troves of Karak Kadrin.
master-rune-of-smiting.body: A weapon inscribed with the Master Rune of Smiting gains the Multiple Wounds (D6) special rule.

master-rune-of-swiftness.description: This rune was first struck by Thurgrom the Hermit, the last runesmith to study Elven crafts.
master-rune-of-swiftness.body: The wielder of a weapon inscribed with the Master Rune of Swiftness gains the Strike First special rule.

master-rune-of-breaking.description: Runesmiths take pride in seeing the inferior works of other races break beneath a hammerblow.
master-rune-of-breaking.body:
Any magic weapon carried by an enemy model that suffers one or more unsaved wounds from a weapon inscribed with the Master Rune of Breaking is destroyed and cannot be used for the remainder of the game.
Note that even if their magic weapon is destroyed, the model is still considered to be armed with a hand weapon.

rune-of-banishment.description: First crafted in the days of the Ancestor Gods, the touch of this potent rune is anathema to the creatures of Chaos.
rune-of-banishment.body: Enemy models with the Warp-spawned special rule cannot make any Ward saves against hits caused by a weapon inscribed with the Rune of Banishment.

wizard-s-staff.description: Throughout the Old World, Wizards carry ensorcelled staffs through which they can channel and direct their powers.
wizard-s-staff.body:
0-1 per Wizard. The bearer of the Wizard's Staff gains a +1 modifier to their Casting roll when attempting to cast an Assailment spell or a Magic Missile.
*Extremely Common

rune-of-might.description: A weapon inscribed with Runes of Might can fell a Giant in a flurry of blows.
rune-of-might.body:
For each Rune of Might inscribed upon a weapon, its wielder has a +1 modifier to their Strength characteristic.
*Rule of Duplication

grudge-rune.description: Grudge Runes seek out the enemies of the Dwarfs with unerring accuracy.
grudge-rune.body:
For each Grudge Rune inscribed upon a weapon, its wielder may re-roll a single roll To Hit of a natural 1 made during the Combat phase.
*Rule of Duplication

rune-of-parrying.description: A weapon with this rune moves like quicksilver to block the attacks of the enemy.
rune-of-parrying.body: Any enemy model that directs its attacks against a model wielding a weapon inscribed with a Rune of Parrying during the Combat phase suffers a -1 modifier to its rolls To Hit.

rune-of-fury.description: A Rune of Fury is an emblem of the anger all Dwarfs feel towards the enemies of their ancestors.
rune-of-fury.body:
For each Rune of Fury inscribed upon a weapon, its wielder has a +1 modifier to their Attacks characteristic.
*Rule of Duplication

rune-of-cleaving.description: This rune was first made for mining tools, to allow them to break through rock with ease.
rune-of-cleaving.body:
Hand weapon only. For each Rune of Cleaving inscribed upon a weapon, its Armour Piercing characteristic is improved by 1.
*Rule of Duplication

rune-of-fire.description: Struck whilst the weapon glows white-hot, a Rune of Fire forever binds the heat of the forge.
rune-of-fire.body: The wielder of a weapon inscribed with a Rune of Fire gains the Flaming Attacks special rule.

wizard-s-familiar.description: Many Wizards keep familiars, supernatural creatures that aid them in their arcane studies. Often, this aid is apparent in the ease with which the Wizard dispels the conjurations of their enemies.
wizard-s-familiar.body:
0-1 per Wizard. The owner of a Wizard's Familiar may apply a +1 modifier to any of their Dispel rolls.
Note that this is a modifier to the result of a roll – it does not negate a roll of a natural double 1.
*Extremely Common

rune-of-striking.description: A weapon with this rune moves to strike the foe's most vulnerable area with an uncanny precision.
rune-of-striking.body:
For each Rune of Striking inscribed upon a weapon, its wielder has a +1 modifier to their Weapon Skill characteristic.
*Rule of Duplication

master-rune-of-slaying.description: The power held within this master rune has sent the likes of Giants, Trolls and even Dragons running for cover.
master-rune-of-slaying.body: When making a roll To Wound against an enemy whose troop type is behemoth with a weapon inscribed with this rune, a roll of 3+ is always a success regardless of the target's Toughness. In addition, a weapon inscribed with this rune gains the Multiple Wounds (D3) special rule.

rune-of-speed.description: This rune enhances its bearer's awareness and quickness, catching unwary enemies by surprise.
rune-of-speed.body:
Hand weapon only. For each Rune of Speed inscribed upon a weapon, its wielder has a +1 modifier to their Initiative characteristic.
*Rule of Duplication

master-rune-of-bursting-flame.description: On contact with the enemy, the shot from weapons inscribed with this powerful rune explodes in a shower of burning fragments.
master-rune-of-bursting-flame.body: If the roll To Hit is successful, a weapon inscribed with this rune causes 2D3 hits to the target enemy unit, rather than the usual one hit.

rune-of-concussive-force.description: Emblazoned upon the ammunition itself, this rune disorientates the enemy with a flash of light and a thunderous burst of sound.
rune-of-concussive-force.body: A unit hit with an attack made by a weapon inscribed with this rune gains the Stupidity special rule until your next Start of Turn sub-phase.

master-rune-of-piercing.description: Projectiles shot by this weapon punch through armour and flesh without slowing, allowing the wielder to cut down swathes of enemies in a single shot.
master-rune-of-piercing.body: A weapon inscribed with this rune has a +1 modifier to its Strength characteristic. In addition, a weapon inscribed with this rune shoots like a bolt thrower, using the Through & Through special rule.

rune-of-accuracy.description: Favoured amongst older Engineers, this rune helps the bearer to ignore distractions and focus in on their target.
rune-of-accuracy.body: A weapon inscribed with this rune does not suffer any negative To Hit modifiers.

rune-of-rapid-fire.description: Thanks to some clever innovation and a specially crafted rune, this weapon can unleash a salvo of rounds in the time it takes similar weapons to fire a single shot.
rune-of-rapid-fire.body: A weapon inscribed with this rune gains the Multiple Shots (2) and Quick Shot special rules.

rune-of-molten-steel.description: This rune empowers the projectile to burn with the heat of the forge as it impacts the enemy.
rune-of-molten-steel.body: A weapon inscribed with this rune gains the Flaming Attacks special rule.

enchanted-rune.description: Simple runic enchantments help otherwise mundane ammunition to punch through magical wards and otherworldly armour.
enchanted-rune.body: A weapon inscribed with this rune gains the Magical Attacks special rule.

master-rune-of-gromril.description: In its purest form, Gromril holds runes better than any other substance in all the world.
master-rune-of-gromril.body: A model wearing armour inscribed with the Master Rune of Gromril has an armour value of 2+, which cannot be improved in any way.

rune-of-iron.description: Worked into suits of armour, the potent Rune of Iron increases the durability of the wearer.
rune-of-iron.body: A model wearing armour inscribed with a Rune of Iron has +1 Wound on its profile.

master-rune-of-adamant.description: The Master Rune of Adamant makes flesh harder than granite and more impervious than steel.
master-rune-of-adamant.body: A model wearing armour inscribed with the Master Rune of Adamant has a Toughness characteristic of 10. This rune cannot be combined with any other Armour runes.

rune-of-fortitude.description: Runes of Fortitude turn flesh to iron and turn aside the enemy's blades with ease.
rune-of-fortitude.body:
For each Rune of Fortitude inscribed upon their armour, a model has a +1 modifier to its Toughness characteristic (to a maximum of 10).
*Rule of Duplication

master-rune-of-balance.description: Forged in the glowing embers of a burning book of spells, this rune hungers after the Winds of Magic.
master-rune-of-balance.body: Anvil of Doom and Dwarf Runesmiths only. Once per turn, the bearer of the Master Rune of Balance may use it when attempting a Wizardly dispel. If they do so, roll an extra D6 when making the Dispel roll and discard the lowest result.

rune-of-preservation.description: The Rune of Preservation was first struck to counter the decapitating blows of Elven swordmasters.
rune-of-preservation.body: A model wearing armour inscribed with a Rune of Preservation is immune to both the Killing Blow and Multiple Wounds (X) special rules. If the wearer suffers an unsaved wound from an attack with either of these special rules, they lose a single Wound.

master-rune-of-calm.description: When the power of this rune is unleashed, the Winds of Magic are stilled, leaving enemy Wizards unable to cast even the most simple of spells.
master-rune-of-calm.body:
The bearer of the Master Rune of Calm can cast the following Bound spell, with a Power Level of 2:
Type | Hex
Casting Value | 8+/11+
Range | Self
If this Bound spell is cast with a casting result of 8 or more, enemy Wizards that are within 18" of this model when attempting to cast a spell must increase that spell's casting value by 2. If this Bound spell is cast with a casting result of 11 or more, enemy Wizards that are within 36" of this model when attempting to cast a spell must increase that spell's casting value by 2. This spell lasts until your next Start of Turn sub-phase.

rune-of-shielding.description: In ages past, entire regiments would march to war bearing shields struck with the Runes of Shielding.
rune-of-shielding.body:
A model wearing armour inscribed with a single Rune of Shielding has a 6+ Ward save against any wounds suffered. For each additional Rune of Shielding, this Ward save is improved by 1.
*Rule of Duplication

rune-of-spellbreaking.description: It is said that this powerful rune was first crafted by Grungni and Valaya working as one.
rune-of-spellbreaking.body:
Anvil of Doom and Dwarf Runesmiths only. Single use. The bearer of a Rune of Spellbreaking may use it instead of making a dispel attempt. If they do so, the spell is automatically dispelled with no Dispel roll required.
*Rule of Duplication

rune-of-stone.description: A simple but brittle rune, the Rune of Stone is the first rune taught to apprentice runesmiths.
rune-of-stone.body:
Single use. For each Rune of Stone inscribed upon their armour, a model may re-roll a single failed Armour Save roll.
*Rule of Duplication

master-rune-of-spite.description: Created to protect the gates of Dwarfen holds, this rune is cunningly used on many other devices.
master-rune-of-spite.body: Each time the bearer of the Master Rune of Spite loses a Wound to an enemy attack during the Combat phase, the unit that made the attack suffers a Strength 5 hit with an AP of -2.

rune-of-luck.description: The runesmith who first struck this rune supposedly acquired a fortune in gold through gambling.
rune-of-luck.body:
Single use. The bearer of a Rune of Luck may use it to re-roll a single failed roll To Hit or To Wound, or to re-roll a single failed Armour Save roll.
*Rule of Duplication

rune-of-passage.description: This rune causes even the most treacherous of terrain to part and become level underfoot.
rune-of-passage.body: The bearer of a Rune of Passage gains the Move through Cover special rule. Any unit joined by the bearer also gains the Move through Cover special rule. Should the bearer leave the unit for any reason, the unit loses this special rule.

rune-of-warding.description: Runes of Warding are potent but fragile, and their magic easily expended all too soon.
rune-of-warding.body:
Single use. Each Rune of Warding gives its bearer a 2+ Ward save against a single wound.
*Rule of Duplication

rune-of-the-furnace.description: Intended to aid Dwarfs working hot forges, this rune has been adapted for use in battle.
rune-of-the-furnace.body: The bearer of a Rune of the Furnace has a 3+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by an attack that has the Flaming Attacks special rule.

rune-of-battle.description: In ages past, even lesser strongholds and fortified mines had a standard bearing this humble rune.
rune-of-battle.body: When calculating its combat result, a unit carrying a standard inscribed with a Rune of Battle may claim an additional bonus of +1 combat result point.

master-rune-of-grungni.description: This rune stirs the Winds of Magic until their swirling forces protect those that march beneath it.
master-rune-of-grungni.body: Battle Standard Bearer only. A unit carrying a standard inscribed with the Master Rune of Grungni has a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered. In addition, whilst within 6" of the model carrying this standard, friendly units have a 6+ Ward save against any wounds suffered during the Shooting phase.

master-rune-of-stromni-redbeard.description: This rune was first carved onto the Battle Standard of Durgin, son of Grindo, son of Grimnir.
master-rune-of-stromni-redbeard.body: When calculating its combat result, any friendly unit within the Command range of the model carrying the standard inscribed with the Master Rune of Stromni Redbeard may claim an additional bonus of +1 combat result point.

rune-of-confusion.description: Under the shadow of this rune, the enthusiasm of charging enemies quickly wanes.
rune-of-confusion.body: Any enemy unit that charges the front arc of a unit carrying a standard inscribed with the Rune of Confusion makes a disordered charge.

master-rune-of-hesitation.description: The presence of this rune causes the enemy to hesitate before the Dwarfen throng and falter in their charge.
master-rune-of-hesitation.body:
An enemy unit that charges the front arc of a unit carrying a standard inscribed with the Rune of Hesitation does not count as having charged for the purposes of choosing which weapon to use or using any special rules it may have.
Note that the unit carrying this rune still counts as having been charged by the enemy unit.

rune-of-fear.description: Those that carry this banner to battle seem to tower over the enemy, looming like mythical giants.
rune-of-fear.body: A unit carrying a standard inscribed with the Rune of Fear gains the Fear special rule.

rune-of-courage.description: This inspirational rune further bolsters the already considerable courage of all Dwarfs near it.
rune-of-courage.body: A unit carrying a standard inscribed with the Rune of Courage automatically passes any Fear or Terror tests it is required to make.

master-rune-of-disguise.description: This rune magically distorts the shape of the war machine, rendering it almost invisible.
master-rune-of-disguise.body: A war machine inscribed with the Master Rune of Disguise is always considered to be behind full cover.

rune-of-skewering.description: During the War of the Beard, the Elves paid dearly for their help in crafting this rune.
rune-of-skewering.body: Bolt throwers only. A bolt thrower inscribed with this rune has a +1 modifier to its Strength characteristic. In addition, no armour save is permitted against wounds caused by a bolt thrower inscribed with a Rune of Skewering (Ward and Regeneration saves can be attempted as normal).

strollaz-rune.description: Tireless by nature, Dwarfs that march beneath Strollaz' Rune become relentless in their advance.
strollaz-rune.body: A unit carrying a standard inscribed with Strollaz' Rune gains the Vanguard special rule.

master-rune-of-immolation.description: Devised so that war machines never fall into enemy hands, this rune is invoked only rarely.
master-rune-of-immolation.body: Cannon only. Single use. If a cannon inscribed with the Master Rune of Immolation loses its last Wound to an enemy attack during the Combat phase, it may be exploded by its crew. Every enemy unit in base contact with this model suffers D6 Strength 5 hits with an AP of -2. The cannon is then removed from play as a casualty.

rune-of-reloading.description: War machines inscribed with this rune are almost sentient in their willingness to allow repairs.
rune-of-reloading.body: A war machine inscribed with a Rune of Reloading can shoot every turn, even if it misfired and malfunctioned during its previous turn.

rune-of-burning.description: Shots fired by a war machine with this rune burst into flames when they strike the target.
rune-of-burning.body: A war machine inscribed with a Rune of Burning gains the Flaming Attacks special rule.

stalwart-rune.description: The crew of this war machine will fight with great boldness to defend their beloved engine of war.
stalwart-rune.body: When calculating its combat result, a war machine inscribed with a Stalwart Rune may claim a bonus of +1 combat result point.

rune-of-forging.description: This rune ensures the war machine is free from imperfections and deadly accurate.
rune-of-forging.body:
Single use. A war machine inscribed with a Rune of Forging may use it to re-roll a single misfire on the Artillery dice.
*Rule of Duplication

rune-of-the-dishonoured.description: This dreadful mark prolongs the shame of the one who bears it.
rune-of-the-dishonoured.body: Daemon Slayers and Dragon Slayers only. Once a model with this runic tattoo is reduced to their last Wound, they gain a 3+ Ward save against any further wounds suffered. However, at the end of the battle, a model with this runic tattoo that has been slain is worth no Victory Points. If it is still alive, the enemy player wins a bonus number of Victory Points equal to 100% of its points cost.

rune-of-endless-battle.description: Those who bear this tattoo struggle to contain their rage once battle begins.
rune-of-endless-battle.body:
During the Combat phase of any turn in which a model with this runic tattoo charged, every attack it makes that causes an unsaved wound allows it to immediately make one additional attack.
Note that any additional attacks that cause unsaved wounds and any unsaved wounds caused by the Impact Hits (X) special rule do not benefit from this special rule.

rune-of-the-reckless.description: Slayers that bear this tattoo fight with a burning and uncontrollable fury.
rune-of-the-reckless.body: A model with this runic tattoo gains the Frenzy special rule and, during the Combat phase, has a +1 modifier to their rolls To Hit. However, enemy models that target this model during the Combat phase also have a +1 modifier to their rolls To Hit.

rune-of-the-hateful.description: This unpleasant tattoo fills its bearer with hate and bitterness.
rune-of-the-hateful.body: A model with this runic tattoo gains the Hatred (all enemies) special rule.

rune-of-blazing-fury.description: The rage of the ancestors burns brightly within this fiery rune.
rune-of-blazing-fury.body: A model with this runic tattoo has the Flaming Attacks special rule.

rune-of-the-dauntless.description: Those marked with this rune seek the deadliest foes to challenge in single combat.
rune-of-the-dauntless.body: A model with this runic tattoo must always issue and accept challenges (if possible). During a challenge, this model may re-roll any failed rolls To Hit.

rune-of-wrath.description: Those that bear this rune upon their flesh are filled with wrath.
rune-of-wrath.body: A model with this runic tattoo has a +1 modifier to its Attacks characteristic.

rune-of-grit.description: The flesh of those marked with this rune takes on the texture of stone.
rune-of-grit.body: A model with this runic tattoo has a +1 modifier to its Toughness characteristic.

battleaxe-of-the-last-big-waaagh.description: Vague legend tells that this huge, beaten battleaxe once belonged to either Gork or Mork. How true this is, there is no way of knowing, but it certainly is a great tool for hitting things with!
battleaxe-of-the-last-big-waaagh.body: Notes: If a natural 6 is rolled for the Extra Attacks (+D6) special rule, the Battleaxe of the Last Big Waaagh! loses the Extra Attacks (+D6) special rule at the end of the current Combat phase.

bigger-choppier-axe.description: While Warbosses love having a big, choppy axe, there is nothing they love more than a bigger, choppier axe!
bigger-choppier-axe.body: Killing Blow, Magical Attacks, Requires Two Hands, Strike Last

da-choppiest-choppa.description: This broad, heavy bladed choppa boasts a wickedly sharp cutting edge. What's more, no amount of relentless chopping through armour and hacking through bone ever seems to dull it.

trollhide-trousers.description: Foul smelling and uncomfortable, Trollhide Trousers possess remarkable regenerative properties.
trollhide-trousers.body: May be worn with other armour. The wearer of the Trollhide Trousers improves their armour value by 1 (to a maximum of 2+). In addition, their wearer has the Regeneration (5+) special rule.

da-akrit-axe.description: In battle, this weapon seems to writhe in the hands of its wielder, seeking out the enemy's most vulnerable spots.
da-akrit-axe.body: Notes: The wielder of Da Akrit Axe may re-roll any failed rolls To Hit made whilst using it. However, this weapon's Strength modifier applies only against enemy models the wielder charged this turn.

armour-of-mork.description: This old and battered armour offers powerful protection against magic.
armour-of-mork.body: The Armour of Mork is a suit of heavy armour. In addition, its wearer has Magic Resistance (-2).

dead-ard-armour.description: This battle-scarred armour is made up of thick armour plates capable of turning aside the most telling of blows.
dead-ard-armour.body: Black Orc Bosses and Orc Bosses whose troop type is infantry, cavalry or chariot only. The Dead 'Ard Armour is a suit of full plate armour. In addition, its wearer improves their Toughness characteristic by 1.

spiteful-shield.description: Possessed by an angry spirit and adorned with an enchanted maw filled with razor-sharp teeth, this shield snaps and snarls at unwary opponents.
spiteful-shield.body: The Spiteful Shield is a shield. In addition, any enemy model that rolls a natural 1 when making a roll To Hit or To Wound against the wielder of the Spiteful Shield during the Combat phase immediately suffers a Strength 4 hit with an AP of -.

martog-s-best-basha.description: Warboss Martog the Mauler was renowned for his vast collection of 'legitimately acquired' weapons. The most prized of which was a massive Dwarfen hammer, covered with intricately carved runes and (since Martog's acquisition of the weapon) plenty of Dwarfen blood.
martog-s-best-basha.body: Notes: The wielder of this weapon has a +1 modifier to its Weapon Skill and Initiative characteristics.

glowy-green-amulet.description: This unimposing green amulet glows ever brighter as it absorbs magic. Sooner or later it is going to explode!
glowy-green-amulet.body:
If the bearer (and any unit they have joined) is the target of an enemy spell, they may use the Glowy Green Amulet instead of making a Wizardly dispel attempt. Roll a D6. On a roll of 2+, the spell is dispelled. However, if a 1 is rolled, the Glowy Green Amulet explodes. The amulet is destroyed and cannot be used again, and its bearer loses a single Wound.
Note that the Glowy Green Amulet cannot be used against a perfect invocation.

effigy-of-mork.description: Be it a string of lucky escapes, arcane enchantment, or perhaps the divine intervention of the cunning (yet brutal) Mork, this small trinket seems to keep the wearer out of danger.
effigy-of-mork.body: Any model that directs its attacks against the bearer of the Effigy of Mork during the Combat phase suffers a -1 modifier to its rolls To Hit.

sparkly-wizard-finda.description: Disappointingly, this arcane gem has never helped find a single sparkly Wizard, though it does shine brightly when used to beat one to a bloody pulp!
sparkly-wizard-finda.body: The bearer of the Sparkly Wizard Finda has the Magic Resistance (-2) and Hatred (enemy Wizards) special rules.

warrior-s-rune.description: Only the most skilled of warriors are permitted to bear this mark upon their flesh.
warrior-s-rune.body: A model with this runic tattoo has a +1 modifier to its Weapon Skill characteristic.

the-big-red-raggedy-flag.description: This tattered banner belonged to the great hero, Rowdy Porker, whose spirit imbues it to this day.
the-big-red-raggedy-flag.body: A unit carrying the Big Red Raggedy Flag has a +1 modifier to its Weapon Skill characteristic (to a maximum of 10). In addition, when calculating its combat result, the unit may claim an additional bonus of +1 combat result point.

the-collar-of-zorga.description: Zorga was a respected War Boar wrangler. When his magical collar was stolen, he became a snack for his porcine pets.
