the-collar-of-zorga.body: Any enemy 'beast of burden' that directs its attacks against the wearer of the Collar of Zorga or their unit during the Combat phase suffers a -1 modifier to its rolls To Hit. For the purposes of this rule, a beast of burden is the mount of any model whose troop type is cavalry, the beast(s) that draw any model whose troop type is chariot, and the mount of any mounted character whose troop type is monster.

porko-s-pigstikka.description: Most of the many spears wielded by Porko and his famous Boar Boyz lie shattered across a thousand battlefields. But this particular spear is special, having never broken nor lost its perfect point.
porko-s-pigstikka.body: Notes: Models whose troop type is cavalry, monster or chariot only. This weapon's Strength and Armour Piercing modifiers apply only during a turn in which the wielder charged. In addition, during a turn in which the wielder charged, Porko's Pigstikka grants them +1 Attack for each rank the enemy unit has.

da-banner-of-butchery.description: This rough-hewn totem has absorbed a great amount of primal Orc fury.
da-banner-of-butchery.body: All models in a unit carrying Da Banner of Butchery have a +1 modifier to their Strength characteristic during a turn in which they charge.

wollopa-s-one-hit-wunda.description: The rebellious Goblin known as Wollopa wielded a wondrous weapon. Yet what he is most remembered for is his turn of speed, being able to easily outpace even the most irate of Orcs.
wollopa-s-one-hit-wunda.body: Notes: Goblin and Night Goblin Bosses only. Single use. Once per game, during the first round of combat, the wielder of this weapon can use it with this profile. At all other times, this weapon counts as a hand weapon with the Magical Attacks special rule.

waaagh-banner.description: Blessed by an Orc Shaman, this banner fills those that march under it with a great sense of urgency.
waaagh-banner.body: A unit carrying the Waaagh! Banner increases its maximum possible charge range by 3" and, when it makes a Charge roll, may apply a +D3 modifier to the result.

da-spider-banner.description: Created by the Forest Goblins of the Rootgrubba tribe, this unsettling banner depicts their fearsome arachnid god, whom the tribe reveres alongside Gork and Mork.
da-spider-banner.body: A unit carrying Da Spider Banner gains the Poisoned Attacks special rule. If the unit already has the Poisoned Attacks special rule, then their attacks will wound automatically on a roll of a natural 5 or 6 To Hit, rather than the usual 6.

da-angry-ladz-flag.description: Those who fight under Da Angry Ladz Flag hurl themselves at the enemy with careless abandon.
da-angry-ladz-flag.body: A unit carrying Da Angry Ladz Flag gains the Frenzy special rule.

backstabber-s-blade.description: Being bigger and meaner than most, Orcs are happy to fight anyone, anywhere. Goblins on the other hand, are far happier sticking the pointy end of their blades into their foe's back.
backstabber-s-blade.body:
Notes: Goblin Bosses and Night Goblin Bosses only. If the wielder of this weapon is engaged with an enemy's flank arc, it may re-roll any failed rolls To Wound. If the wielder of this weapon is engaged with an enemy's rear arc, it may re-roll any failed rolls To Hit and To Wound.
*Extremely Common

necklace-of-blessed-teef.description: Plucked from the jaws of enemies and fashioned into crude jewellery, the teef that hang from this necklace have been blessed by Mork (or possibly Gork) to protect the wearer as they thunder into battle.
necklace-of-blessed-teef.body: The bearer of the Necklace of Blessed Teef may re-roll any Armour Save roll, Ward Save roll or Regeneration Save roll of a natural 1.

da-banner-of-da-nomadz.description: Though their Waaagh! takes them the length and breath of the known world, those who carry this banner seldom seem to tire and are constantly on the move.
da-banner-of-da-nomadz.body: When a unit carrying Da Banner of Da Nomadz makes a Charge, Flee or Pursuit roll, it may re-roll any dice that roll a natural 1, before discarding any dice that are required to be discarded.

banner-of-the-wildz.description: The multitude of natural elements used in the construction of this ramshackle standard seem to possess some minor magical enchantment, allowing those who carry it to traverse through foetid swamps, dense forests and rocky slopes without pause.
banner-of-the-wildz.body: A unit carrying the Banner of the Wildz gains the Move Through Cover special rule.

grisly-trophy-rack.description: Covered in the decaying scalps and flayed skulls of conquered enemies, this totem is a foul reminder of the fate that awaits those who fall to the boss' blade.
grisly-trophy-rack.body: Black Orc Bosses, Orc Bosses, Goblin Bosses and Night Goblin Bosses only. All enemy units within 6" of the bearer of the Grisly Trophy Rack suffer a -1 modifier to their Leadership characteristic (to a minimum of 2).

big-boss-at.description: Orcs and Goblins are easily impressed, and this ornate helmet is particularly impressive. What's more, the Boss insists that wearing it makes them braver and cleverer, which must be true.
big-boss-at.body: During the Command sub-phase of their turn, a character wearing the Big Boss 'At that is not engaged in combat may treat their comrades to some inspiring words by making a Leadership test (using their own Leadership). If this test is passed, until your next Start of Turn sub-phase this character and any unit they have joined gains the Unbreakable special rule.

eadbuttin-at.description: 'Eadbuttin' contests are popular in Orc culture. Especially cunning (or brutal) participants employ magical means to improve their odds.
eadbuttin-at.body:
0-1 per model. An 'Eadbuttin' 'At gives its wearer the Impact Hits (1) special rule. This Impact Hit has an Armour Piercing characteristic of -2.
*Extremely Common

staff-of-baduumm.description: Once carried by the famous Orc Shaman Baduumm, this charred wooden staff still contains large reserves of the raw Waaagh! power that evaporated its namesake.
staff-of-baduumm.body:
The bearer of the Staff of Baduumm applies a +D3 modifier to the result of any Casting roll they make. However, if they roll a natural double 1 or double 6 when making a Casting roll, centre a 5" blast template over the bearer. Every model (friend or foe) whose base lies underneath the template risks being hit and suffering a single Strength 6 hit with an AP of -1. The staff is then destroyed and cannot be used again.
Note that this item's effects are in addition to the effects of rolling a natural double 1 or double 6 when making a Casting roll.

idol-of-gork.description: Before heading into a scrap, Orc and Goblin Shamans will craft small idols of Gork, the most brutal (but cunning) of deities to aid them in crumpin' their enemies and disrupting their magic.
idol-of-gork.body: The bearer of the Idol of Gork increases the range of all of their spells by 3". Additionally, once per turn, the bearer of the Idol of Gork may re-roll a Casting roll.

fungus-wine.description: Night Goblins cultivate many strange fungi, the most potent of which are fermented into mind-altering wines.
fungus-wine.body:
Night Goblin characters only. Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, this character may attempt to distribute Fungus Wine to a unit they have joined by making a Leadership test (using their own Leadership). If this test is passed, until your next Start of Turn sub-phase this character and any unit they have joined gains the Immune To Psychology special rule.
*Extremely Common

glittering-wotnots.description: Supposedly made from the shards of a shattered magic mirror, these gaudy gems hung from a Shaman's staff will sometimes reflect hostile magic back upon its caster.
glittering-wotnots.body: If the bearer (or their unit) is the target of an enemy spell, they may use the Glittering Wotnots instead of making a Wizardly dispel attempt. Roll a D6. On a roll of 1-3, the Glittering Wotnots have no effect and the spell is cast as normal. On a roll of 4+, the spell is reflected back upon the caster and they (and their unit) become the target of the spell. The caster may make a Wizardly dispel attempt.

idol-of-mork.description: On the eve of battle, Orc and Goblin Shamans often craft small idols of Mork, hoping that the most cunning (but brutal) of deities will watch over them.
idol-of-mork.body: The bearer of the Idol of Mork increases their Dispel range by 3". Additionally, once per turn, when attempting a Wizardly dispel, the bearer of the Idol of Mork may re-roll the Dispel roll.

guff-s-windy-banner.description: The banner of Guff's Garrison eternally flutters in an inexplicable breeze. Those that fight in its shadow display remarkable intestinal fortitude.
guff-s-windy-banner.body: A unit carrying the Guff's Windy Banner may re-roll any failed Panic test.

the-black-maul.description: This brutal, spiked cudgel is stained black with the blood of a thousand victims. Those that wield the club for too long become overwhelmed by its thirst for violence.
the-black-maul.body: Notes: Each time a natural 6 is rolled for the Extra Attacks (+D6) special rule, the wielder of the Black Maul suffers a -1 modifier to their Weapon Skill characteristic (to a minimum of 1, and for the remainder of the game).

primeval-club.description: This ancient club, bound in cracked leather and infested with spiders and slugs, has been stained red with blood since the dawn of civilisation and is the bane of all order and hope.
primeval-club.body: Notes: The Strength characteristic of the Primeval Club is equal to the current Leadership characteristic of the model that wields it.

mangelder.description: The Mangelder saps the strength of its victims' minds as well as of their bodies, and those few who survive wounds inflicted by the weapon rarely fight again.
mangelder.body: Notes: The wielder of the Mangelder causes Terror. Any enemy unit that suffers one or more unsaved wounds from the Mangelder suffers a -1 modifier to its Leadership characteristic (to a minimum of 2) until the end of the turn.

the-axes-of-khorgor.description: When the Banebeast Khorgor was slain, his axes were taken by his successor and so they have continued to be passed down through the centuries.
the-axes-of-khorgor.body: Notes: The wielder of the Axes of Khorgor may re-roll any rolls To Wound of a natural 1 made during the Combat phase.

axe-of-men.description: A single, mighty stroke from this fearsome axe can cut even the most powerful warrior clean in half, a sight which emboldens the bearer's followers and horrifies their enemies in equal measure.
axe-of-men.body: Notes: Should the wielder of the Axe of Men kill an enemy character (including champions) in a challenge, they gain the Terror special rule for the remainder of the game.

scimitar-of-skultar.description: The dark, serrated blade of this weapon is engraved with words of power in the Dark Tongue, keeping its biting edge keen and sharp for all time.
scimitar-of-skultar.body: Armour Bane (1), Magical Attacks, Multiple Wounds (2)

heavy-chaos-armour.description: Chaos Armour is a gift of the gods, a symbol of the wearer's status as a true champion of Chaos.
heavy-chaos-armour.body:
Heavy Chaos Armour is a suit of heavy armour. May be purchased and worn by a Wizard, even if they do not have the option to be equipped with armour, a shield or barding, without penalty. In addition, the wearer of Chaos Armour has a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered.
*Extremely Common

da-thinkin-orc-s-at.description: With the overpowering need to bash skulls removed from their mind, the wearer might now think twice about charging headlong into an Empire artillery battery!
da-thinkin-orc-s-at.body: The wearer of Da Thinkin' Orc's 'At improves their Initiative characteristic by 1. In addition, the wearer and any unit they have joined is not subject to the Impetuous special rule.

pelt-of-the-dark-young.description: The Pelt of the Dark Young is shrouded in tendrils of darkness that gather about the wearer.
pelt-of-the-dark-young.body: May be worn with other armour. The wearer of the Pelt of the Dark Young improves their armour value by 1 (to a maximum of 2+). In addition, its wearer (and any unit they have joined) has Magic Resistance (-2).

the-brass-cleaver.description: The Brass Cleaver is said to be an artefact from another realm. Ancient and terrible, its outline blurs with a barely restrained thirst for carnage.
the-brass-cleaver.body: Notes: Enemy models are not permitted an armour, Ward or Regeneration save against an attack made with this weapon if the wielder rolls a natural 6 when making a roll To Wound.

full-plate-chaos-armour.description: Chaos Armour is a gift of the gods, a symbol of the wearer's status as a true champion of Chaos.
full-plate-chaos-armour.body:
Full Plate Chaos Armour is a suit of full plate armour. May be purchased and worn by a Wizard, even if they do not have the option to be equipped with armour, a shield or barding, without penalty. In addition, the wearer of Chaos Armour has a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered.
*Extremely Common

the-fur-of-sharggu.description: When the beast-spawn Sharggu was slain, its hide was roughly cut to make a heavy cloak.
the-fur-of-sharggu.body: May be worn with other armour. The wearer of the Fur of Sharggu improves their armour value by 2 (to a maximum of 2+) against non-magical shooting attacks.

da-hag-s-brew.description: Few are sure on exactly what goes into the foetid drink, but its effect is undeniable, imbuing the drinker with the ability to harness the dank magic of the Troll Hags.
da-hag-s-brew.body: Orc Shamans, Goblin Shamans and Night Goblin Shamans only. In addition to the Lores of Magic they may normally know spells from, the bearer of Da Hag's Brew may know spells from the Lore of Troll Magic.

the-blackened-plate.description: This battered suit of plate mail is blackened with the soot of burning palaces and temples.
the-blackened-plate.body: The Blackened Plate is a suit of full plate armour. In addition, its wearer has a 3+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by an attack that has the Flaming Attacks special rule.

cornucopia-of-corpulence.description: This twisted basket overflows with such abundant filth that the weak might drown in its bounty.
cornucopia-of-corpulence.body: When the bearer's combat is chosen during Step 1.1 of any Choose & Fight Combat sub-phase, enemy models in base contact with the bearer of the Cornucopia of Corpulence must make a Toughness test. If this test is failed, they lose a single Wound.

the-gore-banner.description: Enemies tremble to see the foul sigils daubed upon this blood-drenched standard.
the-gore-banner.body: If a unit wishes to declare a charge against a unit carrying the Gore Banner, it must first make a Leadership test. If this test is failed, the unit cannot charge. It does not move and is considered to have made a failed charge. If this test is passed, the unit can charge as normal.

dark-heart.description: Beastmen rip the still beating hearts from their defeated rivals. In battle, they will feed upon these grisly trophies, claiming the strength of their vanquished enemies.
dark-heart.body:
Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, the bearer of a Dark Heart can consume it. The model immediately recovers one lost Wound.
*Extremely Common

totem-of-rust.description: Little more than a jagged spike upon which the corroded remains of armoured warriors are impaled, the Totem of Rust spreads an all-consuming aura of entropy.
totem-of-rust.body: Every model (friend or foe) within 6" of the model carrying the Totem of Rust suffers a -1 modifier to its Armour Save rolls.

chalice-of-dark-rain.description: It is said that to quaff from this blackened and rotted cup is to command the elements.
chalice-of-dark-rain.body: Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, the bearer of the Chalice of Dark Rain may drink from it. Until your next Start of Turn sub-phase, the range of all enemy missile weapons is halved (rounding fractions up) and enemy war machines cannot shoot.

rune-of-the-true-beast.description: This sigil of pure savagery is carved into the flesh of only the mightiest Beastlords, causing even the greatest of monsters to cower before the unbridled ferocity of this raging predator.
rune-of-the-true-beast.body: Enemy models whose troop type is monster suffer a -1 modifier to their Weapon Skill characteristic whilst within 6" of the bearer of the Rune of the True Beast.

manbane-standard.description: The Manbane Standard is a corpse beset by carrion birds. Any who behold it are filled with the dread that it will be upon their eyes that the birds next feast.
manbane-standard.body: All enemy units within 6" of the model carrying the Manbane Standard suffer a -1 modifier to their Leadership characteristic (to a minimum of 2).

hunter-s-spear.description: Crafted to fell the mighty beasts of the far north, this thick-hafted spear bears enchantments allowing it to penetrate yards of flesh and muscle, skewering the foe through-and-through.
hunter-s-spear.body: Notes: The Hunter's Spear shoots like a bolt thrower, using the 'Through & Through' special rule.

buzgob-s-knobbly-staff.description: The famed Great Shaman Buzgob once attempted to channel so much Waaagh! magic that he vanished in a flash of light, leaving behind only his staff and sticky green mist.
buzgob-s-knobbly-staff.body: Once per turn, the bearer of the Buzgob's Knobbly Staff may re-roll a Casting roll.

the-beast-banner.description: Adorned with shattered beast skulls, the Beast Banner radiates an unquenchable thirst for battle.
the-beast-banner.body: A unit carrying the Beast Banner increases its maximum possible charge range by 3" and, when it makes a Charge roll, may apply a + D3 modifier to the result.

vitriolic-totem.description: This gnarled and twisted bough is hung with the heads of the fallen. From these rotted trophies drips a constant rain of blackened ichor and poisoned blood.
vitriolic-totem.body: A unit carrying the Vitriolic Totem gains the Poisoned Attacks special rule.

horn-of-the-first-beast.description: This immeasurably ancient, fossilised horn is said to be taken from the skull of the First Beast. When it is sounded, Beastmen find the savage fury of their race swelling within their hearts.
horn-of-the-first-beast.body: Unless the bearer of the Horn of the First Beast is fleeing, any friendly unit that is within 18" of this model may use its Leadership characteristic when testing for Primal Fury.

horn-of-the-great-hunt.description: The dissonant blare of this twisted horn summons Beastmen to the blood grounds to hunt and slaughter the weak.
horn-of-the-great-hunt.body: Once per turn, after rolling to determine if a unit with the Ambushers special rule that is currently held in reserve as reinforcements arrives, and if the bearer of the Horn of the Great Hunt is on the battlefield and is not fleeing, you may apply a +1 or -1 modifier to the result.

banner-of-outrage.description: This stolen standard has been befouled and stained as a terrible affront to the enemy. Its presence drives Beastmen to ever more vile extremes of savagery.
banner-of-outrage.body: A unit carrying the Banner of Outrage may re-roll its Leadership test when testing for Primal Fury.

the-soiled-tapestry.description: Dragged through filth, this once-sacred banner is now a symbol of hatred.
the-soiled-tapestry.body: A unit carrying the Soiled Tapestry gains the Hatred (all enemies) special rule. However, all enemy models Hate the unit carrying this banner.

banner-of-the-warped-moon.description: Glowing with Morrslieb's light, creatures of the sky cower before the Banner of the Warped Moon.
banner-of-the-warped-moon.body: Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, the bearer of this banner may attempt to unleash its power by making a Leadership test (using their own unmodified Leadership). If this test is passed, until your next Start of Turn sub-phase enemy units cannot use the Fly (X) special rule.

scourge-of-the-burdened.description: Snatched from the petrified fingers of a cruel wagoner, the threat of this barbed whip inspires swiftness amongst all beasts.
scourge-of-the-burdened.body: The wielder of the Scourge of the Burdened can cast the Call of the Wild spell from the Lore of Primal Magic as a Bound Spell, with a Power Level of 2.

stone-of-spite.description: Contained within this glowing stone is the soul of an Ungor, slain in a hideous ritual. When crushed underhoof, a wave of bitterness and spite is released, banishing the Winds of Magic.
stone-of-spite.body: Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, this character may use the Stone of Spite. Until your next Start of Turn sub-phase, all Wizards (friend or foe) suffer a -2 modifier to their Casting rolls.

skin-of-man.description: The wearer of this flayed and sigil-encrusted human pelt is under a glamour, making them appear no more than a particularly ugly peasant. When the skin is cast aside, the awful truth is revealed.
skin-of-man.body: Beastmen Chieftains and Beastmen Shamans whose troop type is infantry only. The wearer of the Skin of Man gains the Scouts and Vanguard special rules.

blood-of-the-shadowgave.description: When shattered upon the ground, clay jars of Morghur's blood boil and spit, birthing mewling beastlings that consume raw magic from the very air, before fading back into the cursed soil.
blood-of-the-shadowgave.body:
Single use. A Wizard may use this item instead of making a Wizardly dispel attempt. If they do so, the spell is automatically dispelled with no Dispel roll required.
Note that a perfect invocation cannot be dispelled.
*Extremely Common

the-plague-chalice.description: This rotted wooden chalice is filled with a vile brew of blood and pus. Any Shaman that sups from it is wracked with pain, even as raw magic courses through their veins.
the-plague-chalice.body: If the bearer of the Plague Chalice rolls any natural double when making a Casting roll (not including rolls of a natural double 1), the spell is cast as a perfect invocation, regardless of its casting value or of any other modifiers. However, each time the bearer casts a perfect invocation, they suffer a Strength 4 hit with no armour save permitted (Ward and Regeneration saves can be attempted as normal).

cacophonous-dirge.description: The march of the warherd is always accompanied by the raucous droning of pipes so deafeningly loud that it drowns out the instruments of all the foe.
cacophonous-dirge.body: Whilst their unit is within 18" of the bearer of the Cacophonous Dirge, enemy musicians cannot use their "Onwards to Victory!", Steadying Rhythm or Quick Time rules.

hagtree-fetish.description: A crudely carved effigy of a hagtree, this shamanic heirloom can spell doom for the Bray-Shaman's foe when brandished with the appropriate curse.
hagtree-fetish.body: Whenever the bearer of the Hagtree Fetish successfully casts a Magic Missile, they may re-roll any rolls To Wound of a natural 1.

a-blight-of-terrors.description: These malicious spites of gruesome appearance dwell in dark places. They delight in terrifying unsuspecting intruders and take great joy from the horror they instil into their prey.
a-blight-of-terrors.body: This model and any unit it has joined gains the Terror special rule.

a-befuddlement-of-mischiefs.description: Mischiefs appear as glowing orbs of light that dart around the heads of their enemies, befuddling the minds of mortals.
a-befuddlement-of-mischiefs.body: During the Combat phase, a single enemy unit that is in base contact with this model suffers a -1 modifier to both its Weapon Skill and Initiative characteristics.

daemon-heart.description: Pulled still beating from the chest of a shadow-skinned Daemon, this gruesome artefact must constantly consume magic lest it fade to dust.
daemon-heart.body:
When attempting a Wizardly dispel, the bearer of the Daemon Heart counts their Level of Wizardry as being one higher than that of the Wizard whose spell they are dispelling or, in the case of Bound Spells, one higher than that spell's Power Level.
Note that this applies even if it would mean the bearer counts their Level of Wizardry as being lower than it actually is.

jagged-dagger.description: This potent sacrificial tool radiates the pain and anger of a thousand ritual offerings made to the Ruinous Powers.
jagged-dagger.body:
The Jagged Dagger can only be used by a Wizard that has joined a unit. Before making a Casting roll, the bearer of the Jagged Dagger may make a sacrifice. One model belonging to the bearer's unit is immediately removed from play as a casualty. The bearer may then modify their Casting roll by adding the Wounds characteristic of the sacrificed model to the result.
Note that this is a modifier to the result of a roll – it does not negate a roll of a natural double 1.

a-muster-of-malevolents.description: Aggressive defenders of Athel Loren, Malevolents dart through the air in the wake of Asrai arrows, descending upon their victims with needle-like talons and vicious fangs.
a-muster-of-malevolents.body: Wood Elf Nobles and Waystalkers only. An enemy model hit by one or more shooting attacks made by this model's Asrai longbow suffers an additional D3 Strength 2 hits, each with an AP of -. These hits have the Armour Bane (1) special rule.

a-murder-of-spites.description: Spites often hide within the cloaks of their hosts, awaiting the opportunity to attack any who draw too near.
a-murder-of-spites.body: When this model's combat is chosen during Step 1 of the Combat phase, a single enemy unit it is engaged with suffers D3 Strength 2 hits, each with an AP of -1.

a-lamentation-of-despairs.description: These creatures are much feared within Athel Loren, for they only appear in times of woe. Outsiders who feel their gaze upon them experience a deep and unnerving sense of dread.
a-lamentation-of-despairs.body: Unless this model is fleeing, enemy units that are within 6" of this model suffer a -1 modifier to their Leadership characteristic when making a Fear, Panic or Terror test (to a minimum of 2).

goretooth.description: In bloody rituals, Bray-Shamans tear the teeth from the jaws of raging beasts to make amulets that allow them to tap into the primal rage of their victims.
goretooth.body:
In addition to the Lores of Magic they may normally know spells from, the bearer of a Goretooth may know spells from the Lore of Primal Magic.
*Extremely Common

an-annoyance-of-netlings.description: Netlings scurry over their host with feverish abandon. Any enemy that attempts to strike the host will find their weapon snagged in a web of magical filaments.
an-annoyance-of-netlings.body: Whilst this model is engaged in a challenge, its opponent in the challenge suffers a -1 modifier to its rolls To Hit.

a-resplendence-of-luminescents.description: As they bound from branch, to bow, to cloak, Luminescents leave behind a magical spoor. Should they alight upon a weapon of any kind, their presence bestows a minor enchantment.
a-resplendence-of-luminescents.body: This model and any unit it has joined gains the Magical Attacks special rule.

destroyer-of-eternities.description: Imbued with powerful incantations, the great blade of this scything weapon is impossibly sharp and is said to destroy the souls of its victims, denying them any hope of reaching the afterlife.
destroyer-of-eternities.body: Notes: Rather than attacking normally, the wielder of the Destroyer of Eternities may choose to make a special 'Scything' attack. If they do, the enemy unit they are directing their attacks against suffers D6 automatic hits, each resolved using the Destroyer of Eternities' profile.

flail-of-skulls.description: This flail is made from the gilded skulls of conquered enemies. Foes struck by these skulls are lacerated and savaged by their sharpened teeth, and bleed profusely from their wounds.
flail-of-skulls.body: Notes: The Flail of Skulls Strength modifier applies only against enemy models the wielder charged this turn.

serpent-staff.description: Crafted in the likeness of a rearing cobra, this tall, heavy-headed staff writhes with an unnatural life, striking at the enemies of its bearer with venomous fangs.

blade-of-antarhak.description: Those cut by the Blade of Antarhak age by decades in the blink of an eye, their vitality stolen and bestowed upon the wielder of this fell blade.
blade-of-antarhak.body: Notes: The Blade of Antarhak may only be taken by models in a Nehekharan Royal Host Army of Infamy. For each Wound an enemy unit loses as a result of an attack made with the Blade of Antarhak, its wielder immediately recovers a single lost Wound.

warding-splint.description: Protective strips of bronze and iron inscribed with regenerative hieroglyphics are placed across the Liche Priest's shrivelled body, for without their power the armies of the Tomb Kings will crumble.
warding-splint.body: The Warding Splint is a suit of heavy armour which may be purchased and worn by a Liche Priest, even if they do not have the option to be equipped with armour, a shield or barding, without penalty. In addition, its wearer has a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered.

royal-mantle.description: It is said that the wisdom of the kings and queens of Nehekhara is held within these armoured plates, giving counsel to the wearer as they command their warriors on the battlefield.
royal-mantle.body: The Royal Mantle may only be taken by models in a Nehekharan Royal Host Army of Infamy. May be worn with other armour. The wearer of the Royal Mantle improves their armour value by 1 (to a maximum of 2+). In addition, the wearer's My Will Be Done special rule affects all friendly units with the Nehekharan Undead special rule within 6" of them, not just a unit they have joined.

staff-of-aeons.description: A single blow from this accursed weapon can cause armour to rust and tarnish in a matter of moments, leaving those wearing it vulnerable to the Liche Priest's minions.
staff-of-aeons.body: Notes: The Staff of Aeons may only be taken by a Liche Priest in a Mortuary Cult Army of Infamy. Any model that is hit by one or more close combat attacks made using this weapon suffers a -1 modifier to its armour value for the remainder of the game.

armour-of-the-ages.description: Forged from bronze, cooled in blood and plated with gold, this ancient armour can turn aside even the strongest blow.
armour-of-the-ages.body: Models whose troop type is infantry, cavalry or chariot only. The Armour of the Ages is a suit of light armour. In addition, enemy models must re-roll successful rolls To Wound made against the wearer.

crown-of-kings.description: Ancient and ornate crowns are a symbol that servitude extends beyond the bounds of death.
crown-of-kings.body:
Monarch of Nehekhara only. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, the wearer of a Crown of Kings may attempt to resurrect the fallen by making a Leadership test. If this test is passed, a single friendly unit of Skeleton Warriors, Skeleton Archers, Skeleton Horsemen or Skeleton Horse Archers that is within this model's Command range recovers D3+1 Wounds.
*Extremely Common

amulet-of-the-serpent.description: Cast in antique gold with glittering emeralds for eyes, this magical snake amulet laces the weapons of nearby Nehekharan warriors with a fast-acting and deadly venom.
amulet-of-the-serpent.body: The bearer of the Amulet of the Serpent and any unit they have joined gains the Poisoned Attacks special rule.

icon-of-the-sacred-eye.description: The arcane power contained within this unblinking eye guides the arms of those that march beneath it.
icon-of-the-sacred-eye.body: A unit carrying the Icon of the Sacred Eye has a +1 modifier to its Weapon Skill characteristic (to a maximum of 10).

collar-of-shapesh.description: This ornate collar is a powerful charm that trades the life of one for that of another.
collar-of-shapesh.body: Single use. When the wearer of the Collar of Shapesh loses their last Wound, roll a D6. On a roll of 4+, the Wound is not lost. Instead, a single friendly model within the wearer's Command range is removed from play as a casualty.

standard-of-the-cursing-word.description: This potent icon contains a powerful curse, similar to that which protects the mortal remains of the ancient monarchs of Nehekhara.
standard-of-the-cursing-word.body: Battle Standard Bearer only. At the end of any phase in which one or more models in a unit joined by the bearer of the Standard of the Cursing Word lost its last Wound to an enemy attack, the unit that made the attack must make a Leadership test. If this test is failed, the enemy unit suffers D3 Strength 2 hits, each with an AP of -, for each model that lost its last Wound.

mirage-banner.description: Shimmering with the heat of the desert, this banner shifts constantly, confusing the eye of the enemy.
mirage-banner.body: Any enemy model that targets a unit carrying the Mirage Banner during the Shooting phase suffers an additional -1 To Hit modifier.

relic-of-the-desert-sun.description: With their withered, mummified forms vulnerable to open flame, some Tomb Kings placed their faith in the sun god Ptra to protect them.
relic-of-the-desert-sun.body: The bearer of the Relic of the Desert Sun is not subject to the Dry as Dust or Flammable special rules.

the-conqueror-s-blade.description: Many a king and queen, warlord and emperor foolish enough to resist the rule of the Lord of Nehekhara have found their heads parted from their bodies by this wicked weapon.
the-conqueror-s-blade.body: Notes: Whilst engaged in a challenge, the bearer of the Conqueror's Blade strikes a Killing Blow if they roll a natural 5 or 6 when making a To Wound roll, rather than the usual 6. In addition, should the wielder slay the enemy General in a challenge, you win a bonus of 100 Victory Points at the end of the game.

phakth-s-blades-of-justice.description: Crackling lightning arcs from these twin blades as they slice through the ranks of Nehekhara's foes.
phakth-s-blades-of-justice.body: Notes: Models whose troop type is infantry only. Phakth's Blades of Justice grant the wielder +1 Attack for each rank an enemy unit the wielder is engaged with has.

royal-standard-of-settra.description: When Settra's personal banner marches to war, it is an omen of doom for those who stand against him. For the True King of Nehekhara kneels to no one; all shall bow to him or face annihilation.
royal-standard-of-settra.body: The Royal Standard of Settra may only be taken in a muster list that includes Settra the Imperishable and/or Nekaph, Emissary of Settra. A unit carrying the Royal Standard of Settra gains the Hatred (enemy characters) and Terror special rules.

sigil-of-centuries.description: Time behaves strangely around this odd icon, the weight of years slowing even the most agile warriors to a sluggish crawl.
sigil-of-centuries.body: All enemy units within 6" of the model carrying the Sigil of Centuries suffer a -1 modifier to their Initiative characteristic (to a minimum of 1).

shield-of-ptra.description: Bursting from the face of this ornate shield, the radiance of the Sun God Ptra blinds the enemy.
shield-of-ptra.body: The Shield of Ptra is a shield. In addition, any enemy model that directs their attacks against the bearer during the Combat phase suffers a -1 modifier to their Weapon Skill characteristic.

cloak-of-the-dunes.description: This tattered cloak is infused with the magic of the deserts, enabling its wearer to transform into an abrasive storm of sand that cuts through the foe.
cloak-of-the-dunes.body: Models whose troop type is infantry only. The wearer of the Cloak of the Dunes gains the Fly (9) special rule. In addition, any enemy unit the wearer moves over during the Remaining Moves sub-phase suffers D6 Strength 2 hits, each with an AP of -1.

tapestry-of-conquered-lands.description: Woven from the standards of vanquished enemies, this patchwork banner serves as a warning to those who stand against the rulers of Nehekhara.
tapestry-of-conquered-lands.body: Any enemy standard captured by a unit carrying the Tapestry of Conquered Lands is worth 100 Victory Points as a trophy of war.

banner-of-the-desert-winds.description: This tattered banner snaps and waves under the command of a spectral breeze, whose gusts drive forward those who march under it.
banner-of-the-desert-winds.body: Models whose troop type is infantry only. A unit carrying the Banner of the Desert Winds gains the Vanguard and Reserve Move special rules.

icon-of-rakaph.description: Those that march beneath the banner of King Rakaph II are instilled with unrivalled discipline.
icon-of-rakaph.body: Unless it made a charge move, a unit carrying the Icon of Rakaph may perform a single free reform after moving during the Remaining Moves sub-phase.

death-mask-of-kharnutt.description: The expressionless Death Mask of Kharnutt has borne witness to the demise of untold thousands over its long millennia, causing an aura of dread and despair to hang heavily about it.
death-mask-of-kharnutt.body: The wearer of the Death Mask of Kharnutt gains the Terror special rule.

crook-flail-of-radiance.description: These gleaming golden weapons represent the high status of the bearer, and all that enter their presence are humbled by the aura of majesty these weapons convey.

scarab-brooch.description: From far beneath the desert sands, scuttling dead things are drawn towards this blackened brooch.
scarab-brooch.body: When using the From Beneath the Sands special rule, a summoned unit can be placed on the battlefield anywhere completely within 18" of a Liche Priest wearing the Scarab Brooch, rather than the usual 12".

icon-of-rulership.description: The hero's chariot bears a totemic standard that pulses with greatness and proclaims their many victories over their enemies.
icon-of-rulership.body:
Models whose troop type is chariot only. This model doubles its Unit Strength, from 3 to 6. In addition, any Impact Hits caused by this model have an Armour Piercing characteristic of -2 and the Magical Attacks special rule.
*Extremely Common

staff-of-awakening.description: Carried only by the most revered Liche Priests, this powerful artefact amplifies the wielder's already formidable necromantic talents.
staff-of-awakening.body: High Priest only. When the wielder of the Staff of Awakening uses the Arise! special rule on a friendly unit whose troop type is infantry or cavalry, that unit recovers an additional D3 Wounds.

orb-of-ptra.description: Upon uttering a prayer to the mighty Ptra, this orb becomes as bright as the midday sun, confounding enemy archers.
orb-of-ptra.body: Any enemy model that targets this character or any unit they have joined during the Shooting phase suffers an additional -1 To Hit modifier.

hieratic-jar.description: This earthenware jar, sealed with wax and bound with glyphs, contains the magically charged remains of a once-mighty Liche Priest.
hieratic-jar.body:
Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, the bearer of a Hieratic Jar can release the power held within it. The bearer may attempt to resurrect the fallen by using the Arise! special rule twice during this Command sub-phase (rather than the usual once).
*Extremely Common

curse-weaver-wand.description: The power within this accursed wand seeks only to enfeeble the enemies of its wielder.
curse-weaver-wand.body: The bearer of the Curse-weaver Wand gains a +1 modifier to their Casting roll when attempting to cast a Hex spell.

filth-mace.description: This heavy-headed and rust-encrusted mace endlessly oozes a necrotic slime which can sap the strength and vitality of the strongest warriors, causing even minor wounds to become debilitating.
filth-mace.body: Notes: Any enemy model that suffers one or more unsaved wounds from the Filth Mace must immediately make a Toughness test. If this test is failed, the wounded model suffers a -1 modifier to its Toughness characteristic (to a minimum of 1) until the end of the turn.

daemonsword.description: This most deadly of blades is a prison for the essence of a powerful but treacherous Daemon. For all the might it grants its wielder, the Daemon within endlessly strives to be set free.
daemonsword.body: Notes: Every roll of a natural 1 made when rolling To Hit with this weapon results in a hit which must be resolved against the unit the wielder has joined, rather than the enemy. If the wielder has not joined a unit, this hit must be resolved against the wielder.

tablets-of-tahoth.description: These powerful relics of Tahoth's wisdom crumble to dust once their power is spent.
tablets-of-tahoth.body:
A Wizard may purchase up to three Tablets of Tahoth, each of which is single use. Before making a Casting roll, a Wizard may choose to use any number of their Tablets. For each Tablet used, you may apply a +1 modifier to the result of the Casting roll.
Note that this is a modifier to the result of a roll – it does not negate a roll of a natural double 1.
*Extremely Common

obsidian-dread-glaive.description: This cruel weapon has been used to sever heads and limbs in the hands of the Dark Gods' most dangerous champions.
obsidian-dread-glaive.body: Notes: The Obsidian Dread-glaive may only be taken by a model in a Heralds of Darkness Army of Infamy.

chaos-runesword.description: This evil blade was forged from black gromril by the thrice-cursed Dwarf Runesmith Grugni Ironheart, a secret pawn of the Chaos gods.
chaos-runesword.body: Notes: The wielder of the Chaos Runesword has a +1 modifier to their Weapon Skill and Initiative characteristics.

dagger-of-the-dark-pantheon.description: By drawing on the lifeforce of those slain with this wicked weapon, its wielder is able to channel the Winds of Magic far more recklessly.
dagger-of-the-dark-pantheon.body: Notes: For each Wound an enemy unit loses as a result of an attack made with the Dagger of the Dark Pantheon, its wielder may apply a +1 modifier to their next Casting or Dispel roll.

crimson-armour-of-dargan.description: The rich crimson metal of this armour flares into a storm of bloodcoloured light when its wearer wills it, dazzling those who would strike a mortal blow.
crimson-armour-of-dargan.body: Models whose troop type is infantry or cavalry only. The Crimson Armour of Dargan is a suit of heavy armour. In addition, the wearer is immune to the Multiple Wounds (X) special rule. If the wearer suffers an unsaved wound from an attack with this special rule, they lose a single Wound.

spellthieving-sword.description: Forged of magically resistant ores and carved with dire runes of spell warding, the Spellthieving Sword burns and blinds its victims, robbing them of their mage sight.
spellthieving-sword.body: Notes: Any enemy Wizard that suffers one or more unsaved wounds from the Spellthieving Sword immediately forgets a single spell (determined at random) for the remainder of the game.

armour-of-the-damned.description: This ornate suit of Chaos armour shimmers with the eldritch energies of the Chaos Wastes, distorting the wearer's outline and clouding the minds of their foes.
armour-of-the-damned.body: The Armour of the Damned is a suit of full plate armour. In addition, during the Combat phase, enemy models must reroll successful rolls To Hit made against the wearer.

daemonic-platemail.description: This infernal armour writhes with the leering and screeching faces of the daemonic spirits that infest it.
daemonic-platemail.body: Models whose troop type is infantry or cavalry only. The Daemonic Platemail is a suit of full plate armour. In addition, its wearer improves their Toughness and Initiative characteristics by 1.

crown-of-everlasting-conquest.description: The warrior's helmet is crafted into a magnificent crown of spikes and horns which radiate invigorating dark power.
crown-of-everlasting-conquest.body: The wearer of the Crown of Everlasting Conquest gains the Regeneration (5+) special rule.

talisman-of-the-carrion-crow.description: The magical wards that venerate the Crow blesses the wearer with otherworldly resilience and empowers their strikes with deadly poisons.
talisman-of-the-carrion-crow.body: The bearer of the Talisman of the Carrion Crow has the Regeneration (5+) and Poisoned Attacks special rules.

brazen-collar.description: Champions are sometimes gifted with heavy, rune-etched brass collars. Worn around the neck, these marks of favour are potent wards against magic.
brazen-collar.body:
The wearer of a Brazen Collar has Magic Resistance (-2).
*Extremely Common

talisman-of-the-soaring-eagle.description: Those who wear the mark of the Eagle find the potency of their opponents' magic wane in their presence.
talisman-of-the-soaring-eagle.body: The bearer of the Talisman of the Soaring Eagle has the Magic Resistance (-2) special rule. In addition, the bearer has a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by an attack that has the Magical Attacks special rule.

doom-totem.description: A collection of ragged skins strung over a framework of bone, the Doom Totem exudes a potent magic that demoralises and appals all who look upon it.
doom-totem.body: All enemy units that can draw a line of sight to the model carrying the Doom Totem suffer a -1 modifier to their Leadership characteristic.

banner-of-the-gods.description: Forged in the red-lit depths of Zharr-Naggrund, the Banner of the Gods induces dread in the enemy and unshakeable courage in the servants of Chaos.
banner-of-the-gods.body: A unit carrying the Banner of the Gods ignores all negative modifiers to its Leadership characteristic.

chieftain-s-blade.description: The title of Chieftain is earned and kept through triumph in single combat, not by birthright.
chieftain-s-blade.body: Notes: The Chieftain's Blade may only be taken by a model in a Wolves of the Sea Army of Infamy. Whilst engaged in a challenge, the wielder has a +1 modifier to their rolls To Hit.

banner-of-the-dark-powers.description: Pulsing with iridescent light, this banner shields those who march beneath it from all but the most potent magic.
banner-of-the-dark-powers.body: A unit carrying the Banner of the Dark Powers gains the Magic Resistance (-3) special rule.

enkhil-s-kanopi.description: Within this dusty clay vessel resides the wicked heart of the Liche Priest Enkhil. Should it ever be opened, the spirit of the jealous priest consumes the magic of his rivals.
enkhil-s-kanopi.body: Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, the bearer of Enkhil's Kanopi may attempt to unleash its contents by making a Leadership test (using their own, unmodified Leadership). If this test is passed, all Remains in Play spells currently in play are dispelled, including spells cast by friendly Wizards.

mighty-serpent-s-scalemail.description: A dark enchantment wrought in the name of the Serpent has been placed upon the glittering scales of this armour.
mighty-serpent-s-scalemail.body: The Mighty Serpent's Scalemail may only be taken by models in a Wolves of the Sea of Infamy. Mighty Serpent's Scalemail is a suit of heavy armour. In addition, its wearer gains the Strike First special rule.

blasted-standard.description: The Blasted Standard burns with coruscating magical flames that explode outward to consume any missile that comes near it.
blasted-standard.body: A unit carrying the Blasted Standard may re-roll any rolls of a natural 1 when making an Armour Save roll against wounds suffered during the Shooting phase.

taskmaster-s-scourge.description: This devilish weapon is covered in barbed spines, whose bite drives the followers of Chaos into battle.
taskmaster-s-scourge.body: Notes: Models whose troop type is infantry only. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, the wielder of the Taskmaster's Scourge may attempt to urge those around them into battle with a lash of their whip by making a Leadership test (using their own Leadership). If the test is passed, until your next Start of Turn sub-phase, this character and any unit they have joined gain a +D3 modifier to their Movement characteristic (to a maximum of 10).

rod-of-the-damned.description: Forged in the depths of the Realm of Chaos, this infernal rod sunders those who resist the will of Chaos.
rod-of-the-damned.body: The bearer of the Rod of the Damned may cast The Summoning spell from the Lore of Daemonology as a Bound spell with a Power Level of 2.

banner-of-rage.description: Sewn from strings of congealed gore, this banner radiates a bloodlust so strong that those beneath it are goaded into a state of permanent rage.
banner-of-rage.body: A unit carrying the Banner of Rage gains the Frenzy special rule. However, unlike other Frenzied units, this unit cannot lose this special rule.

banner-of-the-baying-hound.description: Those who carry the banner of the Baying Hound race towards their foes, eager to shed the blood of their enemy.
banner-of-the-baying-hound.body: The Banner of the Baying Hound may only be taken by a model in a Heralds of Darkness Army of Infamy. A unit carrying the Banner of the Baying Hound gains the Vanguard special rule.

icon-of-darkness.description: This accursed icon is cloaked in endless shadow, the darkness shielding those who bear it from view as they march.
icon-of-darkness.body: Any enemy model that targets a unit carrying the Icon of Darkness during the Shooting phase suffers an additional -1 To Hit modifier.

bloodskull-pendant.description: Filled with the blood of a Daemon Prince of Khorne, this accursed amulet turns the wearer into a maelstrom of violence.
bloodskull-pendant.body: Models whose troop type is infantry only. Instead of attacking normally, the bearer of the Bloodskull Pendant may choose to inflict a single Strength 8 hit on every enemy model it is in base contact with, each with an AP of -1. These hits have the Killing Blow special rule.

daemon-forged-barding.description: The wicked, hell-forged blades that cover this barding slice and maim the enemy as the rider crashes through their ranks.
daemon-forged-barding.body: Daemon-forged barding may only be taken by a model whose troop type is cavalry in a Heralds of Darkness Army of Infamy. On a turn in which the bearer charged, their mount and all mounts in any unit they have joined have a +1 modifier to their Attacks characteristics.

pendant-of-damnation.description: This pendant burrows deep into the owner's chest and nestles beside their heart, filling them with vitality even as their mortal form inches towards damnation.
pendant-of-damnation.body: Models whose troop type is infantry or cavalry only. The bearer of the Pendant of Damnation gains a +1 modifier to their Attacks characteristic for every Wound they lose.

favour-of-the-gods.description: The Champion bears an obsidian pendant that marks them as having truly earned the favour of the Dark Gods.
favour-of-the-gods.body:
Single use. The bearer of a Favour of the Gods may re-roll the D6 when rolling on the Gaze of the Gods table.
*Extremely Common

helm-of-many-eyes.description: This ornate full face helm has no eyeholes, but is covered with magical eyes that, it is said, can see into the souls and minds of men.
helm-of-many-eyes.body: The Helm of Many Eyes gives its wearer (but not their mount) the Strike First special rule. However, due to the confusing images the helm conjures up, its wearer is also subject to the Stupidity special rule.

sceptre-of-power.description: Those who have carried the Sceptre have enjoyed the thrill of limitless power, but each of them paid a heavy price for the privilege.
sceptre-of-power.body: The bearer of the Sceptre of Power may apply a + 1 modifier to any of their Casting or Dispel rolls. However, should they roll any natural double when making a Casting or Dispel roll, the bearer suffers a single Strength 10 hit with an AP of -3 after the effects of the roll have been resolved.

skull-of-katam.description: The polished skull of the daemonologist Katam constantly whispers its dark secrets into the mind of any Wizard nearby.
skull-of-katam.body:
The bearer of the Skull of Katam and any other Wizard within 3" (friend or foe) may apply a +1 modifier to any Casting roll they make.
Note that this is a modifier to the result of a roll – it does not negate a roll of a natural double 1.

ph-zerakt-s-kanopi.description: It is said that Phâzerakt's spirit can be unleashed from within the ornate vessel in which it is trapped to aid in a mass summoning.
ph-zerakt-s-kanopi.body:
Single use. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, the bearer of Phâzerakt's Kanopi may attempt to unleash its contents by making a Leadership test (using their own, unmodified Leadership). If this test is passed, place a unit of 2D6+3 Summoned Skeleton Warriors on the battlefield anywhere completely within 12" of this model, but not within 1" of any enemy models:
Troop Type: Regular Infantry
Base Size: 25 x 25 mm
Unit Size: 2D6+3
Equipment: Hand weapons and shields
Special Rules: Horde, Nehekharan Undead, Regeneration (6+), Skirmishers
Note that Summoned Skeleton Warriors are not worth any Victory Points.

infernal-puppet.description: Twisting and jerking upon its strings, this eldritch homunculus draws the Winds of Magic into itself, causing them to flow with strange currents that confound the wits of its master's rivals.
infernal-puppet.body: Unless the owner of the Infernal Puppet is fleeing or engaged in combat, they may use it whenever an enemy Wizard that is within 15" of them makes a Casting roll. If they do so, the enemy Wizard must roll an extra D6 and discard the highest result.

grimoire-of-ogvold.description: Ogvold feverishly documented many arcane secrets over the years, hoping that this knowledge would serve the will of Chaos even after his demise.
grimoire-of-ogvold.body: Rather than randomly generating the spells they know, and regardless of their Level of Wizardry, the bearer of the Grimoire of Ogvold knows all seven spells from their chosen Lore of Magic (including the signature spell). However, they can only cast a number of spells equal to their Level of Wizardry per turn.

dark-majesty.description: An air of oppression radiates from the champion, reducing the will of the bravest to that of a craven child.
dark-majesty.body: Unless this character is fleeing, any enemy unit that is required to make a Fear or Terror test whilst within this character's Command range does so with an additional -1 modifier to its Leadership characteristic (to a minimum of 2).

spell-familiar.description: A spell familiar memorises a spell on its master's behalf, constantly rehearsing for its big moment until it is called upon to share its arcane knowledge.
spell-familiar.body:
0-1 per Wizard. The owner of a Spell Familiar knows one more spell (chosen in the usual way) than is normal for their Level of Wizardry.
Note that this does not increase the Wizard's Level.
*Extremely Common

daemon-flesh.description: The Champion's flesh crawls with ætheric energy, turning aside the blows of the enemy.
daemon-flesh.body: This character cannot be wounded by a roll To Wound of 2, regardless of the Strength of the attack.

extra-arm.description: Gifted with an extra arm, the Champion rains many blows upon their enemies.
extra-arm.body: This character (but not their mount) has a +1 modifier to their Attacks characteristic.

tome-of-the-dark-gods.description: This ancient text is filled with the maddening scrawlings and forbidden knowledge of both daemonic and mortal sorcerers alike.
tome-of-the-dark-gods.body: Models with the Mark of Chaos Undivided only. When generating their spells, the bearer of the Tome of the Dark Gods may discard any number of their randomly generated spells. For each spell they discard, they may select any spell from the Lore of Chaos as if they had the corresponding Mark of Chaos.

acid-ichor.description: The Champion's blood is a boiling, acidic ichor. Those who would harm them find themselves splashed with hissing, burning liquid.
acid-ichor.body: For every Wound this character loses during a challenge, their enemy suffers a Strength 4 hit, with an AP of -2.

diabolic-splendour.description: The air around the Champion seethes with chaotic energy, obscuring them from the arrows of the enemy.
diabolic-splendour.body: Models whose troop type is infantry or cavalry only. Any enemy model that targets this character or any unit they have joined during the Shooting phase suffers an additional -1 To Hit modifier.

aura-of-pain.description: The Champion's damned form exudes an aura of pain which wracks their enemies with crippling agony.
aura-of-pain.body: Once per game, when this character's combat is chosen during Step 1.1 of the Choose & Fight Combat sub-phase, a single enemy unit they are engaged with suffers D6 Strength 3 hits, with no armour or Regeneration saves permitted (Ward saves can be attempted as normal).

enchanting-aura.description: An enchanting aura hangs about the Champion, ensnaring the mind and slowing the limbs of enemies that venture too close.
enchanting-aura.body: Models whose troop type is infantry or cavalry only. Enemy units engaged in combat with this character cannot use the Strike First special rule. Enemy models that do not have the Strike First special rule become subject to the Strike Last special rule instead.

master-of-mortals.description: The Champion is worshipped as a god by their mortal followers, who see in them the power of Chaos made manifest.
master-of-mortals.body: Unless this character is fleeing, friendly units of Chaos Marauders and Marauder Horsemen gain a +1 modifier to their Leadership characteristic whilst within this character's Command range (to a maximum of 10).

slug-skin.description: This grotesque gift of the Chaos gods causes the recipient's skin to constantly ooze with a vile, foul smelling slime.
slug-skin.body: Any enemy model that directs its attacks against this model or any unit it has joined during the Combat phase suffers a -1 modifier to its rolls To Hit.

pelt-of-midnight.description: The Beastman's pelt exudes clouds of smokey darkness, hiding them from the eyes of the enemy.
pelt-of-midnight.body: Characters only. Any enemy model that targets this character or any unit they have joined during the Shooting phase suffers an additional -1 To Hit modifier.

poisonous-slime.description: The Champion's flesh is saturated with a toxic slime that seeps from their skin, poisoning anything it touches.
poisonous-slime.body: This character (but not their mount) has the Poisoned Attacks special rule.

many-limbed-fiend.description: Some Beastman grow additional arms, allowing them to unleash even more carnage upon the battlefield.
many-limbed-fiend.body: This model (but not its mount) has a +1 modifier to its Attacks characteristic. However, this bonus attack must be made using an ordinary hand weapon.

sea-raider-s-crest.description: The flags flown by notorious raiders strike fear into the hearts of those who eke out an existence by the sea.
sea-raider-s-crest.body: The Sea Raider's Crest may only be taken by a model in a Wolves of the Sea Army of Infamy. A unit carrying the Sea Raider's Crest gains the Fear special rule. If the unit already has the Fear special rule, it gains the Terror special rule.

crown-of-horns-beastmen.description: A Beastman that sprouts an excessively sharp, large or twisted set of horns is supremely confident in their position at the pinnacle of the Warherd, so obvious are the Dark Gods' blessings.
crown-of-horns-beastmen.body: Characters only. This character and any unit they have joined gains the Stubborn special rule.

muscular-monstrosity.description: The Beastman has been blessed by the Gods of Chaos, and its torso bulges with huge muscles.
muscular-monstrosity.body: This model (but not its mount) has a +1 modifier to its Strength characteristic.

gouge-tusks.description: This Beastman's lower incisors have grown into sharp or excessively large tusks with which they gouge savage wounds into the flesh of their enemies.
gouge-tusks.body: During the Combat phase, the Armour Piercing characteristic of any weapon used by this model (but not its mount) is improved by 1.

unnatural-fortitude.description: Blessed by the Ruinous Powers with great resilience, some warriors' flesh can turn aside steel.
unnatural-fortitude.body: Unless they are wearing heavy armour or full plate armour, models with this Chaotic Trait improve their Toughness characteristic by 1 (to a maximum of 10).

rune-of-the-beast-ascendant.description: The Beastman's horns have twisted into the semblance of a potent daemonic rune. This promise of ascendency to the ranks of Daemonhood fills its followers with courage.
rune-of-the-beast-ascendant.body: Beastman Chieftains only. Unless this character is fleeing, friendly Bestigor, Gor and Ungor Herds gain a +1 modifier to their Leadership characteristic whilst within this character's Command range (to a maximum of 10).

uncanny-senses.description: The Dark Gods gift some Beastman with acute senses, additional eyes or even extra heads, granting them unnaturally fast reactions.
uncanny-senses.body: This model (but not its mount) has a +1 modifier to its Initiative characteristic.

gnarled-hide.description: The Beastman's skin has encysted, forming a dense layer of crusty natural armour as tough as chainmail.
gnarled-hide.body: Models whose troop type is 'infantry' only. This model gains the Armoured Hide (1) special rule.

dark-hearts.description: Those whose souls have been corrupted by the touch of the Ruinous Powers are chilling to behold.
dark-hearts.body: Models whose Troop Type is infantry or cavalry only. If the winning side of a combat includes one or more units in which the majority of models have this Chaotic Trait, each unit that belongs to the losing side suffers a -1 modifier to its Leadership characteristic when making its Break test. Models that have this Chaotic Trait, that cause Terror, or that are Immune to Psychology are unaffected.

brazen-will.description: There are those amongst the hordes of Chaos whose warped minds seem to resist the hostile magic of enemies.
brazen-will.body: Models whose Troop Type is infantry or cavalry only. A unit with this Chaotic Trait gains the Magic Resistance (-1) special rule.

battle-hunger.description: Possessed of an unwholesome thirst for battle, whole regiments race eagerly into the fray.
battle-hunger.body: Models whose Troop Type is infantry only. A unit which consists entirely of models with this Chaotic Trait increases its maximum possible charge range by 2" and, when making a Charge or Pursuit roll, may apply a + D3 modifier to the result.

enhanced-reflexes.description: Gifted with unnatural quickness, some warriors are able to slip the most lethal of blows past the defences of even the most skilled enemies.
enhanced-reflexes.body:
Whilst engaged in combat, models with this Chaotic Trait that choose to fight with a hand weapon gain a +2 modifier to their Initiative characteristic.
Note that this Chaotic Trait only applies to a single, non-magical hand weapon, or an Ensorcelled Weapon, and does not apply to a model's mount (should it have one). If the model is using two hand weapons or any other sort of weapon, this Chaotic Trait ceases to apply.

prophetic-foresight.description: Granted brief glimpses of the future, a warrior may predict the movements of enemy scouts and foresee the arrival of reinforcements.
prophetic-foresight.body: Enemy units that deploy using the Scouts special rule cannot be deployed within 18" of a unit in which every model has this Chaotic Trait (rather than the usual 12"). In addition, enemy units that deploy using the Ambushers special rule may not be placed within 12" (rather than the usual 8") of a unit in which every model has this Chaotic Trait.

spear-of-twilight.description: When this spear strikes, the fury and rage of the wielder is channelled into the body of the foe with appalling and destructive force.
spear-of-twilight.body: Notes: When the wielder of the Spear of Twilight makes a roll To Wound, a roll of 3+ is always a success, regardless of the target's Toughness.

longstriders.description: Covering the ground with an unnatural haste, Longstriders are blessed with a daemon-like speed.
longstriders.body: 0-1 unit per 1,000 points. Unless they are wearing heavy armour or full plate armour, models with this Chaotic Trait gain the Vanguard special rule.

mantle-of-rebirth.description: This enchanted armour fills the wearer with the vitality of spring, instilling them with power and quickly healing their wound.
mantle-of-rebirth.body: The Mantle of Rebirth is a suit of light armour. In addition, its wearer has the Regeneration (5+) special rule.

blades-of-loec.description: The swirling and delicate patterns inscribed into these matched swords assume a life of their own when sunlight falls upon them, dazzling and distracting the bearer's opponent.
blades-of-loec.body: Notes: The wielder of the Blades of Loec may re-roll any failed rolls To Wound.

bow-of-loren.description: Strung with a single hair from the head of Ariel, Queen of Loren, the wielder of the Bow of Loren is the Fey Queen's champion, striking down her enemies with unnaturally swift precision.
bow-of-loren.body: Notes: The Bow of Loren counts as an Asrai longbow. The wielder of the Bow of Loren may make a number of shooting attacks equal to their Attacks characteristic, rather than the usual one. This model does not suffer any modifiers for firing multiple shots.

glamourweave.description: Enemies that view this brooch become entranced by its hypnotic colours and patterns.
glamourweave.body: Enemy models must make a Leadership test before making any rolls To Hit against the wearer of the Glamourweave during the Combat phase. If this test is failed, only rolls of a natural 6 will hit.

helm-of-the-hunt.description: This enchanted great helm imbues its wearer with the furious spirit of Orion himself.
helm-of-the-hunt.body: May be worn with other armour. The wearer of the Helm of the Hunt improves their armour value by 1 (to a maximum of 2+). In addition, the wearer has a +1 modifier to both their Weapon Skill and Attacks characteristics during a turn in which they charge.

cloak-of-tumbling-leaves.description: The wearer draws upon the power of the wind to carry them across the battlefield with great haste.
cloak-of-tumbling-leaves.body: Models whose troop type is regular infantry or heavy infantry only. The Cloak of Tumbling Leaves is a suit of light armour. In addition, its wearer has the Fly (10) and Swiftstride special rule. However, the wearer cannot join a unit.

blades-of-endless-flame.description: All in Athel Loren know how swiftly fire can consume all in its path when left unchecked, which is why the Wood Elves only turn to it under the most dire circumstance.
blades-of-endless-flame.body: Extra Attacks (+1), Flaming Attacks, Magical Attacks

tapestry-of-talsyn.description: Known as the Groves of Eternity, Talsyn is the largest and most prosperous region of Athel Loren, its heraldry a rallying point for all the Asrai.
tapestry-of-talsyn.body: Battle Standard Bearer in a Host of Talsyn Army of Infamy only. A model carrying the Tapestry of Talsyn increases their Command Range to 18". In addition, friendly units within the bearer's Command Range improve their Leadership characteristic by 1 (to a maximum of 10).

banner-of-the-wildwood.description: The malevolence of the spirits that reside within the Wildwood clings to this tattered banner, chilling the souls of those that cast their gaze upon it.
banner-of-the-wildwood.body: A unit carrying the Banner of the Wildwood gains the Fear special rule. If the unit already has the Fear special rule, it instead gains the Terror special rule.

vaul-s-wrath.description: Aggrieved by his fate, Vaul poured much of his rage into this mighty warbow during its creation.
vaul-s-wrath.body: Notes: Once per game, unless the wielder moved during the previous Movement phase, Vaul's Wrath can be shot like a bolt thrower, using the Through & Through special rule.

railarian-s-mantle.description: Woven by the eldest Branchwraiths, this armour is only gifted to one chosen by Athel Loren itself.
railarian-s-mantle.body: Railarian's Mantle is a suit of light armour. In addition, whilst its wearer is within 6" of a woodland terrain feature, they have a 4+ Ward save against any wounds suffered.

hunt-master-s-pride.description: Gifted to those favoured by Orion, this enchanted spear has struck the dark hearts of many beasts over the centuries.
hunt-master-s-pride.body: Notes: The Hunt Master's Pride may only be taken by models in an Orion's Wild Hunt of Infamy. The Multiple Wounds (2) special rule applies only against models whose troop type is monstrous infantry, monstrous cavalry, monstrous creature or behemoth.

daith-s-reaper.description: Amongst the most finely crafted weapons in all Athel Loren, this blade is said to be able to slice through steel without pause.
daith-s-reaper.body: Notes: Enemy models must re-roll any successful Armour Save rolls against wounds caused by this weapon.

banner-of-the-hunter-king.description: The tattered threads of this ancient standard resound with Orion's eagerness for battle.
banner-of-the-hunter-king.body: A unit carrying the Banner of the Hunter King gains the Vanguard special rule.

asyendi-s-bane.description: A malicious spirit dwells within the body of this light and elegant bow, ever eager to punish its wielder if a shot misses its target.
asyendi-s-bane.body: Notes: Asyendi's Bane counts as an Asrai longbow. The wielder of Asyendi's Bane may re-roll a single failed roll To Hit made during the Shooting phase. However, if the re-roll also fails to hit, the wielder suffers a single Strength 3 hit with an AP of -.

merciw-s-locus.description: The eccentric Merciw held the concepts of personal honour and fairness in unusually high esteem.
merciw-s-locus.body: The Strength characteristic of the bearer of Merciw's Locus cannot be modified by any weapon. However, the Strength characteristic of any model that directs its attacks against the bearer during the Combat phase cannot be modified by any weapon either.

banner-of-the-eternal-queen.description: This banner was woven by no lesser hand than that of Ariel, Mage Queen of Athel Loren.
banner-of-the-eternal-queen.body: When calculating its combat result, a unit carrying the Banner of the Eternal Queen may claim an additional bonus of +1 combat result point if it is within 6" of a woodland terrain feature.

banner-of-springtide.description: Adorned with symbols of spring, this standard fills the Asrai with uncanny speed.
banner-of-springtide.body: A unit carrying the Banner of Springtide gains the Quick Shot special rule.

ariel-s-favour.description: A token of the Mage Queen's goodwill, those who bear her gifts are shielded from the baleful magic of their enemies!
ariel-s-favour.body: The bearer of Ariel's Favour has the Magic Resistance (-2) special rule.

banner-of-the-wild-hunt.description: When the Horn of the Wild Hunt sounds, this great banner is unfurled and Orion's warriors feel the call of the hunt echo through their veins.
banner-of-the-wild-hunt.body: The Banner of the Wild Hunt may only be taken by a model in an Orion's Wild Hunt of Infamy. When calculating its combat result, a unit carrying the Banner of the Wild Hunt may claim an additional bonus of +1 combat result point. In addition, the unit may re-roll Pursuit rolls.

wraithstone.description: The screams of all who have met death within the bounds of Athel Loren emit from within this crystal.
wraithstone.body: Unless the bearer of the Wraithstone is fleeing, enemy units suffer a -1 modifier to their Leadership characteristic (to a minimum of 2) whilst within 6" of the bearer.

crown-of-antlers.description: A glittering circlet of gold adorned with a resplendent set of antlers, this exquisite headpiece is as deadly as it is beautiful.
crown-of-antlers.body: The Crown of Antlers gives its wearer the Armour Bane (1) and Impact Hits (D3) special rule. This Impact Hit has an Armour Piercing characteristic of -2.

deepwood-sphere.description: This twisted and thorny orb of ebony wood speaks to the trees in the bitterest words of vengeance and spite, exhorting them to strike down all who intrude upon them.
deepwood-sphere.body: Unless the bearer of the Deepwood Sphere is fleeing or engaged in combat, they may use it when an enemy Wizard that is within 6" of a woodland terrain feature successfully casts a spell. If they do so, no dispel attempt can be made and the spell is cast as normal. Once the spell has been resolved, the enemy Wizard immediately suffers D3 Strength 4 hits, each with an AP of -1.

hail-of-doom-arrow.description: When shot from a longbow, a Hail of Doom arrow splits into dozens of deadly shards.
hail-of-doom-arrow.body:
Single use. Models with Asrai longbow only. A Hail of Doom Arrow can be fired as normal from the bearer's Asrai longbow. If the roll To Hit is successful, place a small (3") blast template so that its central hole is directly over the centre of the target unit. Any model whose base lies underneath the template risks being hit and suffering a single Strength 4 hit with an AP of -1 and the Magical Attacks special rule.
*Extremely Common

wailing-arrow.description: These arrows wail when they draw blood, chilling the soul of even the bravest warrior.
wailing-arrow.body:
Single use. Models with Asrai longbow only. A Wailing Arrow can be fired as normal from the bearer's Asrai longbow. Any unit that suffers an unsaved wound from this shot must make a Panic test as if it had taken heavy casualties.
*Extremely Common

orion-s-favour.description: Those who bear the trinkets gifted by Orion know that their spear will strike true and their arrows will soar unhindered.
orion-s-favour.body: Single Use. The bearer of Orion's Favour can re-roll any failed rolls To Hit and/or To Wound made during the Combat phase.

blight-tipped-arrows.description: Coated in virulent toxins harvested from the depths of the Wild Wood, blight-tipped arrows need only nick the flesh to bring about a slow and painful death.
blight-tipped-arrows.body:
Single use. Models with Asrai longbow only. A Blight-Tipped Arrow can be fired as normal from the bearer's Asrai longbow. If an enemy model suffers an unsaved wound from a Blight-Tipped Arrow, at the beginning of each subsequent Start of Turn sub-phase that model must make a Toughness test. If the test is failed, the model immediately suffers a single wound with no armour or Regeneration saves permitted (Ward saves may be attempted as normal).
*Extremely Common

oaken-stave.description: This crooked staff awakens the power of Athel Loren itself against those enemies that would use their magic to harm it.
oaken-stave.body: Whilst within 3" of a woodland terrain feature, the bearer of the Oaken Stave increases their Dispel range by 3". Additionally, whilst within 3" of a woodland terrain feature, the bearer may roll an extra D6 when making the Dispel roll and discard the lowest result.

orb-of-midsummer.description: At the height of summer, when the great forest is filled with life, the magic of the Wood Elves reaches the peak of its power.
orb-of-midsummer.body: Once per turn, the bearer of the Orb of Midsummer may re-roll a Casting roll.

standard-of-morning-s-chill.description: As the mists cloud the forest before dawn, so too do they now shield those faithful to Athel Loren from harm.
standard-of-morning-s-chill.body: The bearer of the Standard of Morning's Chill can cast the Swirling Mists spell from the Lore of the Wilds as a Bound Spell, with a Power Level of 2.

sigil-of-the-mage-queen.description: Upon the eve of battle, Ariel, beloved Queen of Athel Loren, infuses arcane vessels with a measure of her power. These tokens she gifts to her most favoured mages.
sigil-of-the-mage-queen.body: Single Use. The bearer of the Sigil of the Mage Queen may use it before making a Casting roll. If they do, they may apply a +2 modifier to that Casting roll.

heartwood-pendant.description: Crafted from the heartwood of an ancient oak felled deep within the darkest depths of the great forest, this pendant allows its bearer to tap into the power of Athel Loren itself.
heartwood-pendant.body:
In addition to the Lores of Magic they may normally know spells from, the bearer of a Heartwood Pendant may know spells from the Lore of the Wilds.
*Extremely Common

the-white-sword.description: A legendary blade forged for Aren, one of the first Swordmasters of Hoeth. The White Sword stands as tall as an Elf, yet its wide blade is as light as a willow switch.
the-white-sword.body: Notes: Models whose troop type is infantry or chariot only.

star-lance.description: Forged from the metal of a fallen star, this weapon's graceful lines belie the formidable power it grants its wielder.
star-lance.body: Notes: Models whose troop type is cavalry or monster only. The Star Lance can only be used during a turn in which the wielder charged. In subsequent turns (or if the wielder did not charge) the model must use its hand weapon instead.

wand-of-wych-elm.description: Fashioned from the innately magical Wych Elm tree, this humble wand allows its bearer to easily bend the Winds of Magic to their will.
wand-of-wych-elm.body: Once per turn, if they are within 3" of a woodland terrain feature, the bearer of the Wand of Wych Elm may re-roll a failed Casting roll.

bow-of-the-seafarer.description: Crafted from a single piece of rare silverwood and gifted to lanor of the Sea Guard by Finubar himself, this mighty bow is rumoured to be capable of sinking ships!
bow-of-the-seafarer.body: Notes: The Bow of the Seafarer counts as a Bow of Avelorn. The Bow of the Seafarer shoots like a bolt thrower, using the Through & Through special rule.

armour-of-caledor.description: Every piece of the Armour of Caledor has been taken from the recovered fragments of now-lost armour that was once worn by a mighty Caledorian hero.
armour-of-caledor.body: The Armour of Caledor is a suit of full plate armour. In addition, its wearer has a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered.

blade-of-sea-gold.description: Forged in the crushing depths and honed by crashing waves, this gleaming blade strikes with the unstoppable power of the ocean itself.
blade-of-sea-gold.body: Notes: The Blade of Sea Gold may only be taken by models in a Sea Guard Garrison Army of Infamy.

reaver-bow.description: Some believe this wondrous bow is the same one that was forged for Prince Arathion of Ellyrion a thousand years ago.
reaver-bow.body: Notes: The Reaver Bow counts as a Bow of Avelorn Avelorn. The wielder of the Reaver Bow may make a number of shooting attacks equal to their Attacks characteristic, rather than the usual one. This model does not suffer any modifiers for firing multiple shots.

armour-of-stars.description: Decorated with glittering gems set in deepest blue lacquer, the Armour of Stars is a wonder to behold.
armour-of-stars.body: Models whose troop type is infantry or cavalry only. The Armour of Stars is a suit of heavy armour. In addition, the wearer is immune to the Killing Blow special rule.
